Table Detail Reports
ACCESS_NUMBERS
Primary Keys
EQUIP_UID
Definition
Information on each service to which a customer subscribes.  The service can be a usage service such as fixed line and GSM (receives CDRs and XDRs which are then costed against the service), or a non usage services, such as Radio Paging or Leased Line  Note:  The Equipment table holds details of items of equipment and these two tables use the same unique identifier
Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition
EQUIP_UID

ACCOUNTS_RECEIVABLE
Primary Keys
ACCOUNT_NO,PRIME_UID
Definition
A list of all financial transactions created on Cerillion  A financial transaction is generated as a result of a business event for which a customer is charged, credited or has made a payment.  There are also some other types of transactions:  Reversals - to reverse another transaction. This is used when the original transaction should be cancelled (only unbilled transactions can be reversed) Totals - payment total transactions, representing a sum of a batch of payments made against multiple accounts.

Datatype
Null
Definition

NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Unique id for this record.  Taken from the ACCS uid  range.
TRANS_CODE
VARCHAR2(6)
N
This shows what kind of transaction is represented-for example monthly rental charge, local calls etc.There are many different codes, held in the Transaction Codes table.The first 2 letters represent the type of transaction and can be one of:CH=chargeCR=creditCI=Invisible creditPY=paymentRV=reversed transactionDB=DebitTO=Payment total

CHAR(1)
N
Status of the transaction. These are set values that are maintained by the software. Possible values are:N-NormalR-ReversedD-Referred (cheque payments referred to drawer)

N
Foreign key to either Access Numbers or Equipment table, to identify the equipment/service to which this charge relates.Where a charge can relate to many equipment/service items, then a full list is held in the Bill Access Numbers table.The value can be 0 if the transaction does not relate to an equipment or service (for example, a payment)
SERVICE_CD
CHAR(2)
Y
From the Service Code of the Access Number or Equipment table to which the transaction relates. Set to null for transactions not related to a service or equipment.
PAY_CODE
VARCHAR2(6)
Y
From the Payment Codes table, indicates the method of payment. This is only populated for payment transactions.
PAY_TOTAL_UID
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Foreign key to another row in Accounts Receivable holding a payment total transaction. The payment total has transaction code of TOTAL and is recorded against account number -2. Each invoice payment has a payment total transaction, and each payment total has one or more invoice payment transaction. The payment total represents the sum of all the payments it links to.
REVERSE_AR_UID
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Holds the Prime UID of the transaction in Accounts Receivable that represents the reversal of this transaction.If it is 0 then the transaction has not been reversedReversal transactions cancel out their original transaction by setting the transaction amounts to the negative amount of the original. Transactions are reversed (through back office screens) where they have been created in error, and not included in any subsequent processing-such as billing, account enquiries and so on.
TARIFF_CODE
VARCHAR2(8)
Y
For non-usage transactions, this contains a foreign key to the Tariff Headers table, representing the product to which this transaction relates.For usage transactions, this contains a foreign key to the Usage Tariffs table.The column may be null, for transactions that are not related to a product-for example for adjustments  and invoice payments.The value in the column is taken from a variety of sources-for example for recurring charges from the Equipment Charging table or from a screen for manually created charges.
TRANS_GROUP_UID
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
A Unique Identifier used to group together like transactions into a batch. The following types of transactions can be grouped like this:- Payments - for some paymetn batches this is a foreign key to Transaction Batch- Refunds - Referrals- Reversals- Coin Box Receipts
TARIFF_SX
CHAR(2)
Y
Foreign key to the Tariff Suffix Defs table, indicating the product charge to which this transaction relates. The column will be null for usage transactions, and for transactions that do not relate to a product-such as invoice payments and adjustments.The value in the column is taken from a variety of sources-for example for recurring charges from the Equipment Charging table.
TARIFF_VER
NUMBER(11, 0)
Y
Along with the Tariff Code and Tariff Sx columns, this provides a foreign key to the Tariff Suffix Versions tables, which identifies the charge for this transaction. 
TARIFF_QTY
NUMBER(11, 0)
Y
Indicates the number of items to which this transaction relates.For example, for usage the number of calls or the duration of calls (system parameter dependent). For rental charges the number of items charged for by this transaction-for example a single transaction can represent the rental charge for 10 telephones.

TRANS_EFFECT_DT
DATE
Y
The date of the business event that caused the transaction to be raised. For example, the current date for a transaction created via a screen, or the date of service connection for a connection charge.
BILL_UID
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Foreign key to the Bill History table, to indicate the bill on which this transaction is included. A value of 0 indicates an unbilled transaction that will be included on the next bill (unless it is a reversal or reversed transaction that is never billed).For payments,  the bill on which the transaction is included will be the next cyclical bill after the payment has been entered. Note this is not the same as the bill to which the payment may be allocated in order to pay the bill (this information is held in the Bill Allocation table).This column identifies the bill (whose entry in Bill_History has Statement_YN set to 'N') on which the transaction appears.Thus it is the bill at the TOP of the billing hierarchy. NOTE this means there will be AR rows where the AR.Account_No and AR.Bill_UID do not match a row in Bill_History. Such AR rows will instead have their AR.Account_No and AR.Statement_Bill_UID matching a Bill_History row.
GL11_INCOME_CODE
VARCHAR2(16)
Y
Nominal code against which this transaction is reported. For a charge, it is the source of income for this transaction from Tariff Suffix Versions or Usage Tariffs table.For a discount is will be from the appropriate discount table (Discount Profile, Tariff Discounts, Usage Volume Discount and so on)For a payment it will be from income code recorded against the payment code used for this payment (see Payment Codes table)There are other sources for certain special transactions, documented in the General ledger Interface PFD.
GL11_UPDATE_ST
CHAR(2)
Y
Indicates three things in one value:1) Type of the transaction for General Ledger reporting purpose2) Whether or not it has been processed by the General Ledger interface3) Whether billed or unbilled, banked or unbanked etc. The possible values are:1 - Unbilled and not passed through GL2 - Unbilled and passed through GL3 - Billed and not passed through GL4 - Billed and passed through GL 5 - Billed/Unbilled and not passed through GL6 - Billed/Unbilled and passed through GL7 - Payment and not passed through GL8 - Payment and passed through GL9 - Not processed by GL at all10 - Cost and not processed by GL11 - Not Cost and processed by GL13 - Suspended and not passed through GL14 - Suspended and passed through GL15 - Released and not passed through GL16 - Released and passed through GL17 - Suspended/Released and not passed through GL18 - Suspended/Released and passed through GLNotes1-4 generally apply to charges and credits, which go from 1->2, 2->3, and 3->4. However this depends on the timing of the GL and billing runs 5/6 apply to transactions raised during billing which are therefore never unbilled on Cerillion. They still appear in the GL separately as billed and unbilled.7/8 generally apply to payments9 applies to transactions that are never processed by GL 10/11 generally apply to discount13 - 18 apply to transactions which are not billed due to suspension of the account, or supression of a bill as a result of minimum threshold functionality.  These values are currently only applied if Navision general ledger functionality is configured.

Definition
Provides a list of open Activities for each Diary.· This table is provided for performance only. It is maintained from the Activity table by triggers and is in essence a programmatically controlled index. This enables the getActivitiesForUser/Department APIs to show current activities in a timely manner.Indexing of the activities table does not provide sufficient performance due to the low number of distinct keys Diary UID provides and the multiple values indicating an open activity.

Definition
This table defines each address profile and the CRM control(s) that will be user to enter addresses for each profile.  An address profile is a definition of the sub-set of cerillion address fields that are used to record a particular type of address, plus other aspect of the appearance of an address.
Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition
ADDRESS_PROFILE_UID
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Unique id for each row.  Taken from the ADDRPROF  uid  range.
NAME
VARCHAR2(20)
N
The name of the profile - this is what is displayed in the drop down list of available profiles.
LOOKUP_CLASS_CD
VARCHAR2(10)
N
Determines the address control class that will be used to do a look-up, leave null if this profile does not use positive address look-up.. List of possible values from Codes where Code Tp Cd is 'AP_LOOKUP'
ENTRY_CLASS_CD
VARCHAR2(10)
N
Determines the address control class that will be used to manually enter address details.. List of possible values from Codes where Code Tp Cd is 'AP_ENTRY'
LOOKUP_AND_ENTRY_YN
CHAR(1)
N
Set this to Y when lookup_class is not null AND you want the user to be able to manually enter an address when they cannot locate it with positive address look-up. Be aware that this setting will be inappropriate if the address profile is used to hold address data that is passed to remote interfaces, for example to a line plant system.
OBSOLETE_YN
CHAR(1)
N
Set to Y when an address profile become obsolete, users will then be able to view these addresses but if they need to change the address they will need to use a different non-obsolete profile.
AUTO_SELECT_ON_ONE_RESULT_YN
CHAR(1)
N
Only applicable to lookup profiles.  If the result of the lookup is a single address, the address is automatically selected by the CRM address control.

ADDRESS_PROFILES_COLUMN
Primary Keys
ADDRESS_PROFILE_UID,COLUMN_NAME
Definition
This table defines each of the address columns that comprise an address profile, validation applied to the column data when a user enters it, and master_addresses look-up configuration.
Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition
ADDRESS_PROFILE_UID
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Unique id for each row.  Taken from the XXXX uid  range.
COLUMN_NAME
VARCHAR2(30)
N
The name of the cerillion address table column. The set of allowed values is: ADDRESS_LINE1, ADDRESS_LINE2, AREA_NAME, COUNTRY_NAME, DELIVERY_POINT_ID, ENTRANCE, EXCHANGE_CODE, EXTENSION, EXTERNAL_UID, FLAT_NO, INFORMAL_ADDRESS, PLACE_NAME, POST_CODE, STREET_NAME, STREET_NO
LINE_NO
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Must be unique with in the columns of a profile, used by legacy code (open-road/VB) to format an address.
COLUMN_MAX_LENGTH
NUMBER(11, 0)
Y
If the address profile requires that the address column data must be shorter than the length of the column in the Cerillion addresses table, set that length here. This restricts the length of the string the user can type into the address field on the CRM address control. If it is not set the length of the Cerillion address table column is used.
RESOURCE_ID
VARCHAR2(50)
N
The value that will be shown in the label next to the address field in the CRM address control. It can be normal text - in which case the label will display what you enter here, or to support multiple languages, it can be a CRM resource string. Currently allowed values for the resource string are: "s.blah" NB If you have Openroad screens in your installation you should not use resource IDs in this field, just plain text because the OpenRoad logic cannot convert resourceIds into language appropriate strings.

VARCHAR2(30)
Y
One of the Cerillion reference type codes, this can be any code_tp_cd from the codes table or one of the special hard-coded values found in CRM (speak to development if you need to use a set of values not stored in the codes table).

LOOKUP_RESULTS_COLUMN_ORDER
NUMBER(11, 0)
Y
The positive address look-up address controls display a table of matching addresses called the results table. The results table will only contain columns that have this field populated. The ordering of the address fields in the results table from left to right is controlled by this column. Use a unique set of numbers per profile id.
MASTER_LOOKUP_COLUMN_NAME
VARCHAR2(30)
Y
Used for profiles that do a positive look-up using data in the master_addresses table (address_profiles.lookup_class = 'AddressLookupMasterAddresses', indicates the master_addresses column name that will be used to populate the cerillion address column. The set of allowed values is: EXTERNAL_UID, ADDRESS_LINE1, STREET_NO, FLAT_NO, STREET_NAME, PLACE_NAME, AREA_NAME, COUNTRY_NAME, POST_CODE
MASTER_LOOKUP_CRITERION_ORDER
NUMBER(11, 0)
Y
Used for profiles that do a positive look-up using data in the master_addresses table (address_profiles.lookup_class = 'AddressLookupMasterAddresses'. The master address look-up control displays a set of drop-downs that are populated from the master_address data. Setting this column value will get a drop down displayed showing data from the master_addresses column nominated in master_lookup_column_name. The one with the lowest value in the column will be displayed and populated first and will be populated with a unique set of values from that column in the master addresses table. The second lowest will be displayed second and will be populated with a unique set of values in that column where the first column matches the value selected in the first drop down. Normall you should not need to have this value set for more than 3 columns to produce a manageable number of results in the results table.
LOOKUP_FIELD_NAME
VARCHAR2(30)
Y
Used for profiles that do a positive look-up using the TNAPS/NI or other (like NORLYS) web service (address_profiles.lookup_class = 'AddressLookupTnaps'/'AddressLookupNI'/any other new look up, indicates the TNAPS/NI/other address field name that will be used to pass in query parameters (especially these are search fields). The set of allowed values for TNAPS is empty and for other customer(NI/other like NORLYS), the set of allowed values are the ones from CODES table with code_tp_cd as 'LRADDFIELD'

ADDRESS_PROFILES_COLUMN_COMBO
Primary Keys
ADDRESS_PROFILE_UID,COMBINATION_NO,COLUMN_NAME
Definition
This table defines combinations of mandatory fields for each profile. A profile may have none, one or more than one combination of mandatory address columns. A typical example might be a profile in which the user must always enter post code, town and street or post code, town and building name, in this case you would have 6 rows in this table for that address profile uid, three rows would have combination_no = 1, the other three rows would have combination_no = 2.

ADDRESSES
Primary Keys
PRIME_UID
Definition
Stores all addresses, referenced by a number of tables, for example, Subscribers for billing address, Access Numbers and Equipment for service addesses.The format of address differs according to the country of operation (OPCRY System Parameter). The columns of the table are used to hold different items according to the country. This is documented against each column. (Note the columns prefixed DISP are not documented, as these are copied from the columns without DISP - see below). The UK format is the default if one of the others is not in use.Each element of the address appears twice in this table. The elements prefixed DISP_ store the elements exactly as entered by users on screens, and used for screen display, and on reports and bills. The other elements (with no prefix) are created from the DISP_ elements, and converted into uppercase. This is used when searching for an address. The data entered by the user is converted to upper case and matches to these fields. For example, if the user enters "High Street" or "high street" or "HIGH STREET", they will match against any address with "high street" recorded in either upper or lower case, or as a combination.Client Specific Info-----------------------------For Jersey, add this index:  CREATE INDEX I_A_JERSEY_ADDRESS_ACCESS ON  ADDRESSES (ADDRESS_LINE1, STREET_NO, STREET_NAME) PCTFREE 10 INITRANS 2 MAXTRANS 255 TABLESPACE INDEX01 NOLOGGING STORAGE(INITIAL 64K         MINEXTENTS 1         MAXEXTENTS UNLIMITED         PCTINCREASE 0         FREELISTS 1         FREELIST GROUPS 1         BUFFER_POOL DEFAULT         )

Primary Keys
EQUIP_UID
Definition
Holds details of a discount given to a customer at sales time.  Typically used for large items where a price is negotiated and an agreed discount given.For Adhoc Discounts, a special Tariff Suffix Versions row is created, using the Tariff Code of the discounted item, and the tariff suffix and version recorded on this table. This special version is only used in charging for this discounted item.Adhoc discounts can only be given on Connection and Purchase charges

AGGREGATED_DATA
Primary Keys
AGGREGATED_DATA_UID
Definition
This table holds 'data', grouped by DAY and other criteria (account,equip, APN, tax code/ver, bill date, transaction code, ledger code, country, zone, prepaidYN).It records the volume, charge, tax for each such group, and the time that the group was last updated.It is very similar to USAGE_SUMMARY, but with a different key.This data is created/updated by the Cerillion summarisation_process. The Bill_Uid column is set by Cerillion billing.It is read by the Cerillion  itemization screens.

ALPHABETIC_ENTRY
Primary Keys
PRIME_UID
Definition
Represents an alphabetic entry in a telephone directory. There is one entry per current service (Access Numbers table), and so multiple entries per account. An entry may have sub-entries - for example, a main entry for a hotel, and a sub entry for kitchen, reservation, reception, etc  Replaces the Alphabetic Directory table.

ALTERNATIVE_LANGUAGE
Primary Keys
TEXT_TYPE_CODE,TEXT_CODE
Definition
Enables operators to provide bills or other documents in any language. The table currently supports the use of three languages, usually comprising English and up to two local languages.The former columns English_Text and Alternative_Text have been replaced by the columns Language_1_Text, Language_2_Text and Language_3_Text. Further languages could be supported by adding further columns.The Bill_Lang_Cd column in Subscribers determines which language should be used for each subscriber, referencing the 'LANGUAGE' code type. The 'LANG_MAP' code type can then be used to map these language codes to the Language_1_Text, Language_2_Text or Language_3_Text columns.These columns also supersede the Alternative_Language_Items table, which is not in use.The table has existed in its current form since at least 2002, although some Data Models show the older form. See CER-27184.
Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition

N
A code defining the type of text, e.g. 'BIL' for billing text. First part of primary key.

N
A unique code identifying the text item. Second part of primary key.
UPDATE_COUNT
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Standard column to check for 'hidden update'

VARCHAR2(120)
Y
Text in the first language, as identified by codes of type 'LANGUAGE' and 'LANG_MAP'. This is not necessarily English.

Y
Text in the second language, as identified by codes of type 'LANGUAGE' and 'LANG_MAP'.

Y
Text in the third language, as identified by codes of type 'LANGUAGE' and 'LANG_MAP'.

BASKET
Primary Keys
BASKET_UID,THIRD_PARTY_ACCOUNT_NO
Definition
A basket of catalogue items to be sold, updated or recovered. Created for each sale or change as temporary information held until the sale or change is completed or cancelled. In the future it will be possible to park a sale for reviving at a later date. It is the temporary nature of the data in these tables that is the reason for the lack of the standard Update_Count column. They are single user usage for a given basket.

BASKET_ITEM_INFO
Primary Keys
SALES_INFO_UID
Definition
Links the Sales Information stored to the Basket and with client understood tags. Information store for an individual product prior to the basket being committed, at which point these become Access_Numbers or Equipment rows.Under CPC-1078/CPC-1373, this now contains all of the information that was saved in Sales_Information, but in an easier to understand form.

Null
Definition

ACCESS_NO
VARCHAR2(256)
Y
Ringing line number, as will appear in a number of CDRs. Generated automatically at sales times from the Unalloc_Access_Numbers table, or entered manually by the user. For non-telephony services, it is the identifier of the usage that appears in CDR/XDR/EDR records, to match the call/event record with a subscriber. Added for CPC-1078/CPC-1373.
EXCHANGE_CD
VARCHAR2(10)
Y
Code representing the network element to which the lin is connected. At most sites, the exchange will be the host switch unit on which the line is provisioned. The value will match that in the corresponding field in Unalloc_Access_Numbers for the access number. Values from Codes where Code_Tp_Cd = 'EXCHANGE', but the value will also correspond to that in Unalloc_Access_Numbers for the access number.  Added for CPC-1078/CPC-1373.
LINE_TP_CD
CHAR(4)
Y
The type of line to which the access numbers should be allocated. For example, for mobile services there may be a line type per dealer or service provider, or for telephony, different line types for analogue, ISDN and Centrex. Used in allocation of numbers from Unalloc_Access_Numbers table, and also in the interface to the line plant application. Values from Codes where Code_Tp_Cd = 'LINE_TYPE', but the value will also correspond to that in Unalloc_Access_Numbers for the access number. Added for CPC-1078/CPC-1373.

LINE_PLANT_RESERVATN_STATUS_CD
VARCHAR2(10)
N
The status of the request to reserve a circuit on the line plant inventory system. Values from table codes where Code_Tp_Cd = 'LP_RSRV_ST'.A value of 'NOT_INVOKD' (the default) means the request has not been invoked. The value INVOK_FAIL is set when the interface has failed to send the request; this value allows the system to try again at a later date. The value INVOKED is set when the request has been successfully sent even when the request failed on the line plant system. When the value is INVOKED the system will not try again to send the request.

BASKET_USER_DEFINED_COLUMN
Primary Keys
SALES_INFO_UID,TABLE_NAME,COLUMN_NAME
Definition
Table to store sales-related columns, primarily on the Access_Numbers and Equipment tables, although it could be used for other tables also. At the time when the information is added, an Equip_Uid for the sales item has not yet been generated in the Access_Numbers or Equipment table, hence the data cannot be added to the User_Defined_Column table, and the need for a separate table. There must, however, be a row in the Basket_Item_Info table, to which this data pertains, and having the Sales_Info_Uid value shown in this table. The structure of the table is identical to that of User_Defined_Column, except that Sales_Info_UID replaces Participant_UID and forms the first part of the primary key. As with User_Defined_Column, each table-name/column-name combination must be defined in the User_Defined_Column_Defn table.Added for CPC-1373.

BATCH_RUN_REQUESTS
Primary Keys
PRIME_UID
Definition
Used to spawn server processes such as work order completion and various reports from the GUI.  The GUI software inserts a row in this table at various points. The most common are when the last step of a work order is completed and a request to run work order completion (WOP0503S02) is created, and from the reports manager MRP0403S where a variety of batch and report processes (as defined in Batch Jobs) can be initiated.  The Job Watch process looks for new rows (the frequency of this check is set by System Parameter CONDB) and starts the appropriate process with the parameters stored in the table columns. Use of table enhanced in CDM19 to include support for the Scheduler.

BILL_ACCESS_NUMBERS
Primary Keys
Definition
During bill generation process many charges can be merged into one accounts receivable transaction, for example, the rental charge on 6 identical telephones. Although transactions are merged, individual access number information is still required for bill printing.  The list of access numbers merged is recorded here.The table can also hold transactions merged from equipment table in which case there may not be Access Number information.
Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition
AR_UID
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Uid of transaction-foreign key to Accounts Receivable. The other columns are a list of access numbers merged in this one transaction
EQUIP_UID
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Foreign key to the Access Numbers or Equipment table. This links to the service/equipment merged in to the AR transaction.
ACCESS_NO
VARCHAR2(256)
N
Access number to be printed on the bill. This is the same as Access No on Access Number matching the Equip Uid, and is repeated here for performance reasons to avoid having to re-read Access Numbers table. Is set to spaces if link to Equipment table.
PBX_SX
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
The private branch exchange number of an access number, to be printed on the bill,-will be zero if not a PBX line. This is the same as PBX Sx on Access Numbers matching the Equip Uid, and is repeated here for performance reasons to avoid having to re-read Access Numbers table. Will be 0 if link to Equipment table.
BILL_ALLOCATION
Primary Keys
DEBIT_BH_UID,AR_UID,CREDIT_BH_UID
Definition
Used for recording all allocations to debit bills. Two different entities can be allocated to a debit invoice (1) a payment (2) a credit invoice. This table acts as a link between payments (PYAC) in Accounts Receivable or credit invoices in Bill History and the debit invoices they are paying in Bill History. Created by billing and payments processing.  A single payment can be allocated to several bills, and a single bill can be paid by several payments.

BILL_CYCLE_PARAMETERS
Primary Keys
BILL_CYCLE_CODE
Definition
Defines billing cycles: a way of splitting customers into more manageable groups so that it is not necessary to bill all customers at once. Holds information on frequency and the next billing date for each billing period cycle code.The Bill Cycle Control table controls allocation of subscribers to bill cycles.Each bill cycle has a date for which bills are created, regardless of when the bill generation process is run
Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition

Y
Description of bill cycle-E.g. Monthly GSM Residential.
LAST_ST
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
The stage that the bill cycle got to last time it was run. This is updated during billing.0 indicates success; either the billing run completed successfully, or it was not run at all (eg for a new bill cycle).Other values indicate that the bill run is incomplete, either because it stopped for some reason, or it is still running. If it stopped, then it needs to be re-started. The higher the value, the further billing reached or has reached.1: Initial success (updates to bill_cycle_parameters to advance the cycle dates have been done and committed to DB).2: Bills generated.3: Bill Summary Report created.4: Bill Transactions Daybook complete.5: Report on items not billed complete.
LAST_DT
DATE
N
Last date of bill cycle. This is not the last date it was run, but the last date on which it was due to be run. For a new bill cycle, Last_Dt is calculated from the Next_Dt minus the Frequency.
NEXT_DT

The next date for which the bill cycle is to be run

CARRIER_SELECTION_DESTINATION
Primary Keys
RULE_UID,CARRIER
Definition
Defines the carriers associated with a rule and their weights (for random allocation).For each rule, we can have one or more carrier_selection_destination rows: the sum of all their weights must be 100. If there is only a row, then the weight must be 100.
Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition
RULE_UID
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Rule which this carrier is associated with. Foreign key to Carrier Selection Rule.
CARRIER
VARCHAR2(10)
N
Destination carrier. This is modelled as a Cerillion exchange code, and therefore valid values are Codes with Code Tp Cd = 'EXCHANGE'.
WEIGHT
NUMBER(3, 0)
N
Integer between 1 and 100. If less than 100, it expresses the weight for random allocation, i.e. the probability that this carrier is selected. The sum of weights for a given Rule UID must equal 100, or if there is only one carrier for the Rule UID, its weight must be 100.

CASH_DRAWERS
Primary Keys
DRAWER_NO
Definition
Holds a record of shop tills that are open, or have been open recently, and a record of transactions that have gone through the till, to check that there has been no keying error. A user may not have more than two drawers open at once - one of these is of status suspended. Cash Drawers are opened when a user starts a new EPOS session (or records a bill payment through Back Office screen PAR10201S)Cash Drawers are closed from the End of Day Banking screen (PAR10701S) and subsequently deleted after having been reconciled and included in the Cash Book Report (PAR10703R).

CDR_SUPPLEMENTARY_SERVICES
Primary Keys
TRANSFER_TYPE,SS_TYPE
Definition
Operators do not often charge for use of supplementary services (call forwarding etc), but details of their usage is contained in the CDR files and is processed by Cerillion. In order to avoid having to set up zero rated tariffs for all of these services and to ensure that they do not cluter up the COS0507R rejection report, details of the service codes can be entered into this table - they will then be filtered out of the body of COS0507R and reported in a summary at the bottom of that report instead of individually.

CODE_KEYS
Primary Keys
PRIME_UID
Definition
Used to hold relationships between different Cerillion tables, and then map the value the relationship defines onto a value. This is best illustrated by an example.  Requirement to generate a message on the bill based upon  a customer's bill cycle (Bill Cycle Code from Subscribers) and town (Area Names from Addresses)  Bill marketing messages are held in Bill Cycle Parameters in the Cycle Message column  A new table consisting of Bill Cycle Code, Area Name and Message would satisfy the requirement. This table and Code Key Classes enables it to be satisfied without creation of a new table.  Each row in this table represent a unique combination of key values - in this case each combination of Bill Cycle Code (in Key Val 1) and Area Name (in Key Val 2). The table assigns each combination a unique class id and then use this uid in the Code Key Classes table.
Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition
PRIME_UID
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Unique id for this key combination.  Taken from the CODEKEYS uid  range. In the example in the table definition, each row used for holding Bill Cycle Code/Area Name combinations will have the same Prime UID.
CLASS_UID
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Unique Id for the combination of key values. In the example in the table definition, each different combination of the values of Bill Cycle Code and Area Name will have it's own Uid. Foreign key to Code Key Classes.
NAME
VARCHAR2(500)
N
Description of the code key combination-for example 'Messages by Area'
KEY_VAL_1
VARCHAR2(10)
N
Value of the first key field-for example a Bill Cycle Code value
KEY_VAL_2
VARCHAR2(10)
N
Value of the second key field-for example an Area Name value
KEY_VAL_3
VARCHAR2(10)
N
Value of the third  key field. NULL if not used
KEY_VAL_4
VARCHAR2(10)
N
Value of the fourth key field. NULL if not used
KEY_VAL_5
VARCHAR2(10)
N
Value of the fifth key field. NULL if not used
KEY_VAL_6
VARCHAR2(10)
N
Value of the sixth key field. NULL if not used
VALUE
VARCHAR2(240)
Y
Value associated with this set of key values. In the example, the bill message to be associated with the Bill Cycle Code in Key Val 1 and the Area Name in Key Val 2.
UPDATE_COUNT
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Standard column to check for 'hidden update'
CODES
Primary Keys
CODE_TP_CD,CODE
Definition
This table is used throughout the Cerillion system to store codes with descriptions - for example it holds many of the codes displayed as options for selection from pull-down lists in Cerillion screens.The table can also be used to hold automatically generated codes, following the pattern 'CC0000000n' where n is taken from Unique Identifiers where the Identifier Tp Cd matches the codes Code Tp Cd value.*** The data in this table is defined by the Codes.xls spreadsheet in the Data Model. ***
Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition
CODE_TP_CD
VARCHAR2(10)
N
Code Type. Used to group different codes into a type, for example, all the different account types (business, residential and so on) have individual rows with Code_Tp_Cd = 'ACCOUNT'. The code types themselves should be defined as codes of Code_Tp_Cd = 'CODE_TYPES'.Codes of Code Type 'ID_TP_CD' are code types for the Numeric_Codes table.  Codes of Code Type 'FUNCT_CODE' have been superseded by the Function_Codes table.
CODE
VARCHAR2(10)
N
One of the possible codes for this particular Code Tp Cd.
CODE_DES
VARCHAR2(80)
N
Description of this code (the description usually appears on screens, and not the code itself).
CODE_CHARS_MAX
NUMBER(11, 0)
Y
Maximum length of this particular code type.(This column does not appear to be in use. It is only meaningful in the context of the 'CODE_TYPES' row for the Code Type, where it could limit the length of all codes of the given Code Type. It is recommended to set the column value to 10 for all new codes and code types.)
CODE_CATEGORY_CD
CHAR(2)
N
The category of the code. List of possible values in Codes, where Code Tp Cd is 'CODE_CAT', which are:CO: 'Configuration' or Customer-defined codes (this is the column default).SY: System Codes, which cannot be updated by the customer and are required for Cerillion to function.ID: Identification Codes. These are ones automatically generated by Cerillion application (this is not widely used).
UPDATE_COUNT
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Standard column to check for 'hidden update'

An operator will have to log the completion of the action later on CRC0306S to mark it as complete. [and set Complete Dt in Cur Collect Plan Actions]
AUTO_FUNCTION_CD
CHAR(4)
Y
The code of an automatic collection action. Specific Cerillion processes handle each automatic action, and the full list is below:REMD - Reminder letter produced by CRC0501RLGCD - legal letter produced by CRC0504RTOSA - Suspend or take off services (CRC0506R)WOFF - Write Off account (CRC0505S)TMSV - Recover All Services (CRC0509R)
MINIMUM_ACCOUNT_BALANCE
FLOAT(126)
N
When the action is processed, this threshold is compared to the current balance of the customer (not the overdue amount of the invoice for which the collection plan was started), if the current balance is less than the threshold then the step is not processed and the current collection plan is stopped.This is used to ensure actions are only performed when it is economic to do so.Defaults to 0.

Indicates if a message is to be placed on the bill to warn that if they do not pay their bill their service will be terminated, and the termination date. This will be output at bill printing time if an action with Auto Function Code of TOSA is due in the future.

CUSTOMERS
Primary Keys
CUSTOMER_UID
Definition
Holds customer level details for each customer in the system.This table is maintained by CRM functionality.One and only one customer must own each account in the Cerillion system, as held in the Subscribers table. However, a customer can have multiple accounts (e.g. a residential account and a business account).From CDM19 / Cerillion 2_1_00 onwards, and in the Product Kernel, the relation between Customers and Subscribers, formerly a foreign key from the customer_uid column in the Subscribers table, is defined by rows in the Relation_Instance table. DB_AMENDS
Primary Keys
Definition
Holds a record of all database upgrade scripts run on the database, in order to have a record of all changes made to database objects - such as tables, indexes, views etc - and also changes to key configuration data, such as system parameters, codes etc.Database scripts provided for upgrades between Cerillion data models or for CPCs and JIRAs, should normally include SQL to insert a record into the DB_Amends table.There is no primary key or unique index on this table; therefore, if a script has been run more than once, for some reason, each run will have a separate record in the DB_Amends table.

DEFAULT_WORK_TASK_LIST_PARAMS
Primary Keys
DEF_WORK_TASK_LIST_UID
Definition
Holds a list of default work tasks for a combination of:- Product or Product Group  (ie defualt for a specific product [tariff_headers] or for a group of products [tariff_groups])- Action, this identifies the type of wokr (eg provide, recover, trouble ticket)- Occurrence - defines whether the list is for the first of an item on an order or a subsequent item on the order - eg if providing two identical services at the same address, then we only need to run a cable to the premises for the first occurrnec, but we need to install and test serice for both occurrences. Currently assumes will only be defined to be against first or subsequent occurrecn - eg can not have a different list for first, second and third occurrence.Not all combiantions need a deafult list - eg some products may not have a default list, some product/action combinations etc
Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition

DISCOUNT_EXTENDED_ALLOWANCE
Primary Keys
ACCOUNT_NO,DIS_PROFILE_UID,PERIOD_START_DATE,PERIOD_END_DATE,EQUIP_UID
Definition
Snapshot of the unbilled discount call itemisation for home subscribers only. The information has been gathered via the Cerillion ciu_upload_unbilled_discount process and is added to on a 'daily' basis. Every time the process is run it will truncate the appropriate records and reinsert the unbilled discount information. Added for CPC-860.The column ALLOWANCE_BILLED should be named ALLOWANCE_ROLLOVER_BILLED, as it shows the amount of rolled over allowance from this period, which has been billed in future periods.As an example, consider a discount with 60 free minutes per month. Assume 20 minutes rolled over from previous period and 25 minutes used in this period, so that only 5 mins of this period's allowance have been used, and 55 mins can be rolled over. The values for this period will be:ALLOWANCE = 60ALLOWANCE_USED = 5ALLOWANCE_ROLLOVER = 55ALLOWANCE_ROLLOVER_USED = 0ALLOWANCE_BILLED = 0Now assume discounting runs in the second period and 15 minutes have been used. The values in the first period are updated as follows:ALLOWANCE_ROLLOVER_USED = 15Now assume discounting runs again and a further 85  minutes have been used (100 mins in total for the second period).  The rolled over allowance of 55 is completely used up and the customer has also used 45 mins of the second period's allowance. The values in the first period are updated as follows:ALLOWANCE_ROLLOVER_USED = 55And in the table for the second period we will have:ALLOWANCE = 60ALLOWANCE_USED = 45ALLOWANCE_ROLLOVER = 15ALLOWANCE_ROLLOVER_USED = 0ALLOWANCE_BILLED = 0Now when billing runs at the end of the second period, values in the first period are updated as follows:ALLOWANCE_BILLED = 55
Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition
ACCOUNT_NO
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Account number that holds the discounted service.equipment. Foreign key to Subscribers table.
DIS_PROFILE_UID
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Disocunt profile of the disocunt for which these extra parameters are defined. Foreign key for Discount Profile
PERIOD_START_DATE
DATE
N
Start date of allowance
PERIOD_END_DATE
DATE
N
End date of allowance
EQUIP_UID
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Identifies service or equipment the discount applies to. Foreign key to either Access Numbers or Equipment 
ALLOWANCE
FLOAT(126)
Y
Allowance provided for period. This and the following allowance fields may be in minutes, seconds, money, or number of calls, depending on the type of discount.
ALLOWANCE_USED
FLOAT(126)
Y
Amount of allowance used in this period - excludes any rollover amount used from previous months.
ALLOWANCE_ROLLOVER
FLOAT(126)
Y
Amount of allowance available to be rolled over in to future periods
ALLOWANCE_ROLLOVER_USED
FLOAT(126)
Y
Amount of rollover used in future periods - this amount gets updated as it is used up in future periods.
ALLOWANCE_BILLED
FLOAT(126)
Y
This column is mis-named. It is actually the amount of rollover from this month that has been billed in future months. The difference between this and ALLOWANCE_ROLLOVER_USED is that ALLOWANCE_BILLED is only updated after billing, while ALLOWANCE_ROLLOVER_USED is updated during discounting.
ROLLOVER_PERIODS
NUMBER(11, 0)
Y
The number of subsequent periods in which a single allowance can be rolled over. 0 means no rollover. 1 would mean one period's rollover, so that if say 40 mins are rolled over from the first period, but only 25 mins are used in the second period, then the remaining 15 mins are lost, although the full 60 mins allowance from the second period is rolled over into the third period.
ROLLOVER_BFWD
FLOAT(126)
N
ROLLOVER_BFWD_USED
FLOAT(126)
N
ROLLOVER_CFWD
FLOAT(126)
N

VARCHAR2(80)
N
Name of the filter - for example Peak Time. The time period that is Peak Time would then be defined in Discount Filter Values. Discounts using this field would then only apply to calls made during peak time.

DISCOUNT_FILTER_VALUES
Primary Keys
FILTER_UID,FILTER_TP_CD,FILTER_VALUE
Definition
Holds all filter values for the script based discounting used from Cerillion 2.0.This makes filtering more flexible than for non-script based discounting, as new types of filters can be added to Discount Filter Names, whereas previously we used separate table per filter type. 
Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition
FILTER_UID
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Identifies the filter type that this value is defined for - foreign key to Discount Filter Names.
FILTER_TP_CD
VARCHAR2(10)
N
A code indicating the type of filter - list of possible values from Codes where Code Tp Cd is FILTERTYPE. Examples would be TIMEPERIOD representing a filter on the Time Period of the call, or DISTBAND representing a filter on calls to a specific distance band.
FILTER_VALUE
VARCHAR2(80)
N
The value of the filter, whose format depends upon the filter type. For example, to apply a filter such that a discount is only given on calls made during peak hours, we would have the following values in this table:Filter UID - links to Discount Filter Name for Peak TimeFilter Type - TIMEPERIODFilter Type - Set to the Timeplan UID in Timeplans that represents peak time.Note for filter type EVENTS, the format is 'source, type, action'  (three integers separated by commas).

DISCOUNT_VOLUME
Primary Keys
DIS_VOLUME_UID
Definition
This table holds the definitions of volume based discounts.  The volume type is variable according to the Volume Tp Cd and Volume Unit Tp Cd.  This means that this table can be used to create many varied discounts.Popular destination discounts within this table have a Volume Tp Cd and Volume Unit Tp Cd of 'DSCCHGORDR'.  A popular destination discount where the most popular number gets a 20% discount and then next 9 get 10% and the next 10 get 5% would require three entries.Popular destination discounts have no calendar frequencies they are for the last bill cycle and expire immediately.  Therefore they have a Dis Cal Freq UID and Dis Expiry Cal Freq UID of 0. Popular destination discounts charge step method is always 'SINGLE'. 
Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition

FUNCTION_CODE,TYPE_CD,VALUE
Definition
This table is used to define what functionality (represented by a function code) is available, dependent upon another parameter. For example, what function codes are available for tariff action codes of 'GSM', to allow only GSM related functions to be made available to GSM services.If the function code is not present in the table, then the functionalty it represents is always available.*** The data in this table is defined by the FunctionCodeApplicability.xls spreadsheet in the Data Model. ***
Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition
FUNCTION_CODE
VARCHAR2(100)
N
The function code that identifies the piece of functionality to be made available.
TYPE_CD
VARCHAR2(100)
N
The item of data which will determine if the functionality is available. If System_Parameter_YN is 'N', this will be a code of type 'APPLTYPECD', which will itself be a code type, and the Value will be a code of this type for which the functionality will be available.  These codes can be concatenated using +.  If System_Parameter_YN is 'Y', Type_Cd will be the name of a system parameter, and Value the value of the parameter which makes the functionality available. 
VALUE
VARCHAR2(240)
N
The Value of the Type for which the functionality will be made available.For example, if set to 'GSM' and Type is 'TARFACTCD' (Tariff Action Code), then the functionality is available to equipment/services that have a tariff with a tariff action code of 'GSM'.
SYSTEM_PARAMETER_YN
CHAR(1)
N
Indicates if the value in Type_Cd is a system parameter. Default is 'N'.
CREATE_YN
CHAR(1)
N
Function code applicability enables CREATE. Only applies to purpose_code 'O' function codes and where system_parameter_yn = 'N'
READ_YN
CHAR(1)
N
Function code applicability enables READ. Only applies to purpose_code 'O' function codes and where system_parameter_yn = 'N'
UPDATE_YN
CHAR(1)
N
Function code applicability enables UPDATE. Only applies to purpose_code 'O' function codes and where system_parameter_yn = 'N'
DELETE_YN
CHAR(1)
N
Function code applicability enables DELETE. Only applies to purpose_code 'O' function codes and where system_parameter_yn = 'N'

GAMTEL_GL_EXTRACT_CFG
Primary Keys
Definition
Filter configuration data for Gamtel-specific General Ledger extract. The output is for import into Gamtel's Access Accounts system, so it is very specific to Gamtel.This table actually contains two separate distinct type of data: (1) account_no is null and the rest populated, (2) account_class_cd null and the rest populated. Therefore this table is actually two distinct tables merged together, one without account_no field, the other without account_class_cd field. The second is relevant to the Nominal Ledger extract only. The first one contains all filter data, the other contains all the account numbers for which a Nominal Ledger extract is wanted.
Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition

N
One of two extract output files: "Sales Ledger" or "Nominal Ledger"
ACCOUNT_CLASS_CD

Y
Filters to be applied on the input data.Account Class Cd is a filter on Subscribers.Account Class Cd -  Example values: "F%", "LN".
ACCOUNT_NO
NUMBER(11, 0)
Y
Account Number to filter by - foreign key to Subscribers
GL_ACCOUNT_CODE
VARCHAR2(16)
N
Value to assign to the "Customer Code" field of the extract.

GENERAL_COLUMN_CRITERIA
Primary Keys
TABLE_NAME,COLUMN_NAME,AVAILABLE_TYPE_CD,AVAILABLE_VALUE
Definition
Provides a means of restricting the availability of User Defined Dields based on standard criteria.The absence of a row in this table for a Table and Column Name allows the user defined field to be seen. The presence of one or more rows in this table for a Table and Column name means that at least one type and value pair must be met to allow the column to be shown.Similar in functionality to Function Code Applicability. Uses an identical set of type codes and values. 
Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition
TABLE_NAME
VARCHAR2(30)
N
Name of table with which user defined column is associated.
COLUMN_NAME
VARCHAR2(30)
N
A unique name that doesn't match with any column names in use on the table. Increased to 62 chars for CPC-691, reduced back to 30 chars for CER-28163.
AVAILABLE_TYPE_CD
VARCHAR2(10)
N
The type for which the restriction will be lifted. For example,TARFACTCD. The list of type codes is obtained from Codes with a Code Tp Cd of 'APPLTYPECD'
AVAILABLE_VALUE
VARCHAR2(10)
N
The value for which the restriction will be lifted. For example GM-POST
UPDATE_COUNT
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Standard column to check for 'hidden update'.

TAP_EXPIRY_DAYS
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
A number of days after which a TAP file is deemed to be missing. for example, if set to 7 and a TAP file is not received for over 7 days from this partner, it is deemed to be missing. Default is 30.
RAP_EXPIRY_DAYS
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
A number of days after which a RAP file is deemed to be missing. for example, if set to 7 and a TAP file is not received for over 7 days from this partner, it is deemed to be missing. Default is 30.
TAP_MISSING_HOURS
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Used to verify the TAP IN file is missing or not. For example, the TAP Missing Hours is set to 6 (hours), the sequence number in database is 105 and received at 09:00 23/09/2003, the incoming sequence number is 107 and received at 11:00 23/09/2003, the 106 is treated as 'delayed' and the tap take on process does not report a missing TAP on this file. And after 15:00 23/09/2003 if the 106 is still not received, when validating next tap in file, the missing TAP will be generated in the RAP file. Default is 6.

SINGLE_SDR_VALUE

N
This is NOT the value of one SDR so a value of 0.5 does not mean that the price would by half this number in local currency. It is the reverse: the value of the local currency in SDRs. So a value of 0.5 means that the local currency is worth only half of an SDR. The number of SDRs is divided by the rate to get the price on local currency-in this case 10 SDR/0.5 = 20.

Definition
The high level grouping of the usage tariff sets available to the per second itemisation pricing processes.  This table defines the version history of these tariff setsNote that the usage type code and tariff group code on this table have a one-to-one relationship - for a given usage type code, there can only be one tariff group code, although there may be more than one version of the tariff group code.This table has many-to-many relationships with other tables, as the other table do not hold both elements of the primary key  - just the Tariff Group Code.To further complicate matters, some other table use usage_tp_cd as a foreign key to this table (e.g. Usage Sales Tax History).

GSM_VIRTUAL_CORRESPONDENTS
Primary Keys
VIRTUAL_CORRESPONDENT_UID,ROAMING_CORRESPONDENT_UID
Definition
Holds details of a virtual correspondent. These are used where a Home Operator "owns" entities acting as 'virtual' operators.Each virtual operator can generate TAP files to send to any of the Operator's roaming partners. Virtual operators so not receivde TAP files from the roaming patrners - only the Home Operator received TAP IN files.This is used for Manx Telecom where they enable passengers on cruise ships to make calls. Each ship is a virtual operator, and passengers from any roaming partner can make a call on the ship, The TAP file generated for the virtual operator includes all calls made by passengers on the ship.
Columns

Datatype
Null
Definition

ROAMING_CORRESPONDENT_UID
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Defines the roaming partner - foreign key to GSM Correspondents. Each roaming partner has a row in this table for each virtual operator

HIGH_SPEND_PRE_PAYMENTS
Primary Keys
PRE_PAYMENT_UID
Definition
Contains a list of payments taken as a bill pre-payment where the account has a high level of unbilled usage. These pre-payments are converted to standard invoice payments at the next billing run, and allocated to that billing run's bill. Any overpayment is then allocated to older unpaid bills, or left as unallocated. Balance of pre-payments on an account is held on the Subscribers table.

Primary Keys

Definition
The table contains a list of IBAN NATIONAL IDs that are not allowed in IBANs. Any IBANs that contain such IBAN NATIONAL IDs are invalid. This list allows financial institutions to detect invalid IBAN payments before sending them out, and to allow corporations to detect incorrectly generated IBANs.

INVENTORY_CODE
Definition
This table holds the inventory definition and details.  The screen Inventory populates this table. The information is read by EPOS, Work Order and Trouble Ticket processes, and the Inventory process to associate an Inventory when an item is sold, returned or replaced. 
Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition
INVENTORY_CODE
VARCHAR2(10)
N
Unique code that defines the Inventory
INVENTORY_DESC
VARCHAR2(80)
N
The name of the inventory
INVENTORY_TYPE_CD
VARCHAR2(10)
N
The inventory type. List of possible values in Codes table, where Code Type is 'INVEN_TYPE'. The Inventory Type can be Central, Transit or Local.
BUSINESS_UNIT
VARCHAR2(10)
Y
Business unit.
BUSINESS_UNIT_GL_ACCOUNT
VARCHAR2(255)
Y
Business unit GL account

INVENTORY_EXPORT_CODE
Primary Keys
TARIFF_CODE,ACC_CATEGORY_CD,INVENTORY_ACTION_CD
Definition
This table holds the Inventory Account Strings (which we will call Inventory Export Codes) which are  similar to Nominal Ledger Codes, used for inventory transactions. The screen Inventory Export Codes populates this table. The information is read by the Inventory process when inserting into Inventory Interface.One record should exist in this table for each combination of Tariff Code, Customer Category and Action Code
Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition
TARIFF_CODE
VARCHAR2(8)
N
Identifies the product, foreign key to Tariff Headers
ACC_CATEGORY_CD
VARCHAR2(10)
N
The Customer Category as on the Subscriber to whom the sale has been made. For non-account sales in EPOS the code recorded in the system parameter CATPR is used. List of possible values in Codes table, where Code Type is  'CATEGORY'.
INVENTORY_ACTION_CD
VARCHAR2(10)
N
The Inventory Action-List of possible values in Codes table, where Code Type is 'INV_ACTION'.  For this table only Sale, Repair or Replacement is used.
ACCOUNT_STRING_1
VARCHAR2(10)
Y
Inventory Ledger Code (Part 1). For XAL, this is the Account part of the Inventory Account String.
ACCOUNT_STRING_3
VARCHAR2(10)
Y
Inventory Ledger Code (Part 3). For XAL, this is the Purpose part of the Inventory Account String.
ACCOUNT_STRING_4
VARCHAR2(10)
Y
Inventory Ledger Code (Part 4). For XAL, this is the Specification part of the Inventory Account String.
INVENTORY_INTERFACE
Primary Keys
Definition
This table is the main table for the Inventory Interface functionality, providing the interface between Cerillion and an Inventory Application. This table is populated by a utility module inform_inventory_interface called from the Work Order, EPOS, Trouble Tickets and Inventory  (Items Delivery) processes. Each row represents one transaction that affects stock held in the operator's inventory (e.g. sell to customer from inventory, add to inventory etc)

ITEM_USAGE_EXP_BATCH_CONTROL
Primary Keys
ACCOUNT_NO
Definition
Controls the batch no for a given account no in the Itemised Usage Export Batch table. Batch No and Daq Day No will determine the values of Batch No and Start Day Day No respectively, in the next record added to Itemised Usage Export Batch for the given account. Added for CPC-1124.
Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition
ACCOUNT_NO
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Account no for which usage is being exported. Foreign key to Subscribers table. Primary key.
BATCH_NO
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Batch no for the next batch that will be generated for the account, being the last batch no for this account plus one.
DAQ_DAY_NO
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Start DAQ Day No of the next batch for this account, derived from the End DAQ Day No of the last batch for this account.

ITEMISED_AMOUNT
Primary Keys
IU_NUMBER,IUA_NUMBER
Definition
Holds both chargeable and non-chargeable monetary amounts (charges and discounts), associated with specific usage. Identifies which 'part' of the usage was charged or discounted, and why. Added for CPC-810.
Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition
IU_NUMBER
NUMBER(20, 0)
N
UID of the Itemised Usage record. Foreign key to the Itemised Usage table. First part of the primary key on this table.
IUA_NUMBER
NUMBER(20, 0)
N
UID of the Itermised Usage Amount. Second part of the primary key on this table. Values directly from the Oracle sequence ITEMISED_AMOUNT_SEQ_NO (does not use the Unique Identifiers table).
AMOUNT
FLOAT(126)
N
Amount including any tax. Negative for credits.
AMOUNT_REASON_CD
VARCHAR2(10)
N
The reason the amount was raised. Values from the Codes table where Code Tp Cd = 'AMOUNTREAS'.
BAL_TRANS_AMOUNT_DIGITS
NUMBER(20, 0)
Y
Significant digits of a balance transaction amount.Together with BAL_TRANS_AMOUNT_EXP, this defines a balance transaction amount.Example: Amount = 1.175BAL_TRANS_AMOUNT_DIGITS = 1175BAL_TRANS_AMOUNT_EXP = -3If this column is populated then  BAL_TRANS_AMOUNT_EXP must also be populated.
BAL_TRANS_AMOUNT_EXP
NUMBER(11, 0)
Y
Exponent value of a balance transaction amount.Together with BAL_TRANS_AMOUNT_SIGITS, this defines a balance transaction amount.If this column is populated then  BAL_TRANS_AMOUNT_DIGITS must also be populated.
BAL_UID
NUMBER(20, 0)
Y
For balance adjustment entries, this links to BALANCE.BAL_UID
CHARGEABLE_YN
CHAR(1)
N
Set to Y if the amount is to be billed either against the account, or billed to another operator via TAP Out. Set to N if the amount is not billable, and is for reference only. 
CHARGED_QUANTITY
NUMBER(20, 0)
Y
Quantity of calls for which the amount applies. Note that this could be different from the Quantity column, due to the unit size.
DIS_PROFILE_UID
NUMBER(11, 0)
Y
The Discount Profile UID, if the amount is due to a discount. Foreign key to the Discount Profile table. Note: if this value is supplied, then the Tariff Code Uid must be null.
DISCOUNT_TOTAL
FLOAT(126)

Amount of charge already discounted by rating.
INCOME_CODE
VARCHAR2(16)
Y

OFFSET
NUMBER(20, 0)
Y
The offset, from the start of the call, for which this amount applies. E.g. from the start of the call, or from the fifth minute, or from the second megabyte.
QUANTITY
NUMBER(20, 0)
Y
The quantity to which this amount applies, e.g. for 10 minutes, or for 1 Gigabyte. This might be different from the value in the Charged Quantity column, which indicates the number of calls covered by the amount.
SALES_TAX_CODE
CHAR(3)

DATE
N

TAX
FLOAT(126)

NUMBER(11, 0)

ITEMISED_AMOUNT_ERROR_LOG
Primary Keys
Definition
The USAGE_LOADER stores information about failures to load data here, and this is then transferred to an error file. This table contains only transitory data and does not require backup or archive. The ORA_xxx$ column names and data types are defined by Oracle. Added for CPC-810.Data is automatically loaded by Oracle during a SQL session to record rows within a transaction that failed. Other rows may have succeeded. Used by the 'LOG ERRORS' functionality.This table differs from Itemised Usage Error Log in that the errors relate to Itemised Usage Amount rows.The index is on IU_NUMBER, IUA_NUMBER and ORA_ERROR_NUMBER$. However, IU_NUMBER and IUA_NUMBER must come after the Oracle-defined columns and therefore appear as the final columns.
Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition

NUMBER
Y
Oracle error code.
ORA_ERR_MESG$
VARCHAR2(2000)
Y
Oracle error text.
ORA_ERR_ROWID$
ROWID
Y
Oracle rowid.
ORA_ERR_OPTYP$
VARCHAR2(2)
Y
Oracle info.
ORA_ERR_TAG$
VARCHAR2(2000)
Y

NUMBER(20, 0)
N
Row number of the usage record.
IUA_NUMBER
NUMBER(20, 0)
N
Row number of the usage amount record.
ITEMISED_AMOUNT_EXTERNAL
Primary Keys
Definition
External table, mapped by Oracle to a transaction file, so that SQL can be used to read data, and transfer it to 'real' tables. This means that the SQL generated under the 'DDL' tab does NOT include all that is required, as an extra 'external organisation' clause is required. For this reason the DDL for this table is disabled, and the PreSQL must be used to generate table SQL.

Datatype
Null

ITEMISED_AMOUNT_NO_EXTERNAL
Primary Keys
Definition
External table, mapped by Oracle to a transaction file, so that SQL can be used to read a list of usage numbers (IU_NUMBER, IUA_NUMBER  rows), and apply changes to those rows in the Itemised Account table. This means that the SQL generated under the 'DDL' tab does NOT include all that is required, as an extra 'external organisation' clause is required. For this reason the DDL for this table is disabled, and the PreSQL must be used to generate table SQL.

ITEMISED_PARTIAL_EXTERNAL
Primary Keys
Definition
External table, mapped by Oracle to a transaction file, so that SQL can be used to read data, and transfer it to 'real' tables. This means that the SQL generated under the 'DDL' tab does NOT include all that is required, as an extra 'external organisation' clause is required. For this reason the DDL for this table is disabled, and the PreSQL must be used to generate table SQL.

ITEMISED_PARTIAL_NO_EXTERNAL
Primary Keys
Definition
External table, mapped by Oracle to a transaction file, so that SQL can be used to read a list of usage numbers (IU_NUMBER rows), and apply changes to those rows in the Itemised Partial table. This means that the SQL generated under the 'DDL' tab does NOT include all that is required, as an extra 'external organisation' clause is required. For this reason the DDL for this table is disabled, and the PreSQL must be used to generate table SQL.

ITEMISED_REJECT
Primary Keys
IU_NUMBER
Definition
Table holding rejected Itemised Usage data. Added for CPC-810.The tables Itemised Usage, Itemised Partial and Itemised Reject contain the itemised call data previously held in Unix files. The three tables have the same columns and foreign keys but different indexes.

ITEMISED_REJECT_EXTERNAL
Primary Keys
Definition
External table, mapped by Oracle to a transaction file, so that SQL can be used to read data, and transfer it to 'real' tables. This means that the SQL generated under the 'DDL' tab does NOT include all that is required, as an extra 'external organisation' clause is required. For this reason the DDL for this table is disabled, and the PreSQL must be used to generate table SQL.

ITEMISED_REJECT_NO_EXTERNAL
Primary Keys
Definition
External table, mapped by Oracle to a transaction file, so that SQL can be used to read a list of usage numbers (IU_NUMBER rows), and apply changes to those rows in the Itemised Reject table. This means that the SQL generated under the 'DDL' tab does NOT include all that is required, as an extra 'external organisation' clause is required. For this reason the DDL for this table is disabled, and the PreSQL must be used to generate table SQL.
Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition
IU_NUMBER
NUMBER(20, 0)
N
Primary key column. Unique for each call across the three tables Itemised Usage / Itemised Partial / Itemised Reject. Values directly from the Oracle sequence ITEMISED_USAGE_SEQ_NO (does not use the Unique Identifiers table).
ITEMISED_REJECT_NO_TEMP

ITEMISED_USAGE_ERROR_LOG
Primary Keys
Definition
The USAGE_LOADER stores information about failures to load data here, and this is then transferred to an error file. This table contains only transitory data, and does not require backup or archive. The ORA_xxx$ column names and data types are defined by Oracle. Added for CPC-810.Data is automatically loaded by Oracle during a SQL session to record rows within a transaction that failed. Other rows may have succeeded. Used by the 'LOG ERRORS' functionality.The index is on IU_NUMBER and ORA_ERROR_NUMBER$. However, IU_NUMBER must come after the Oracle-defined columns and therefore appears as the final column.
Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition

Y
Oracle error code.
ORA_ERR_MESG$
VARCHAR2(2000)
Y
Oracle error text.
ORA_ERR_ROWID$
ROWID
Y
Oracle rowid.
ORA_ERR_OPTYP$
VARCHAR2(2)
Y
Oracle info.
ORA_ERR_TAG$
VARCHAR2(2000)
Y

NUMBER(20, 0)

Start date/time of the batch.
END_TIMESTAMP
DATE
Y
End date/time for the batch.

DAQ day when data acquisition begins for the batch.

NUMBER(11, 0)
N
DAQ Day No when data acquisition ends for the batch.

DATE
N
Date/time of earliest call in the batch.
MAX_CALL_DT
DATE
N
Date/time of latest call in the batch.
INTERFACE_VERSION
NUMBER(3, 0)
N
Format version number of the data files to be produced.
TOTAL_FILES
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Total files produced in the batch.
TOTAL_NORMAL_RECORDS
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Total no of records that are exported to normal files in the batch. These records will have call dates between the Start DAQ Day No and End DAQ Day No.
TOTAL_EXCEPTION_RECORDS
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Total no of records that are exported to exception files in the batch. These records will have call dates after the End DAQ Day No for the batch, or (less likely) before the Start DAQ Day No for the batch.
TOTAL_SKIPPED
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Total no of calls rated between the Start DAQ Day No and the End DAQ Day No but which could not be exported due to a problem with the data causing the call to be rejected. This number may include calls with call dates within the DAQ period which would have been exported to normal files were it not for the rejection, and calls with call dates outside the DAQ period which would have been exported to exception files were it not for the rejection. It is the date of rating, not the call date, which places a rejected call in the Total Skipped.

ITEMISED_USAGE_EXTERNAL
Primary Keys
Definition
External table, mapped by Oracle to a transaction file, so that SQL can be used to read data, and transfer it to 'real' tables. This means that the SQL generated under the 'DDL' tab does NOT include all that is required, as an extra 'external organisation' clause is required. For this reason the DDL for this table is disabled, and the PreSQL must be used to generate table SQL.

Datatype
Null

NUMBER(20, 0)

Primary key column. Unique for each call across the three tables Itemised Usage / Itemised Partial / Itemised Reject. Values directly from the Oracle sequence ITEMISED_USAGE_SEQ_NO (does not use the Unique Identifiers table).

ITEMISED_USAGE_NO_EXTERNAL
Primary Keys
Definition
External table, mapped by Oracle to a transaction file, so that SQL can be used to read a list of usage numbers (IU_NUMBER rows), and apply changes to those rows in the Itemised Usage table. This means that the SQL generated under the 'DDL' tab does NOT include all that is required, as an extra 'external organisation' clause is required. For this reason the DDL for this table is disabled, and the PreSQL must be used to generate table SQL.
Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition
IU_NUMBER
NUMBER(20, 0)
N
Primary key column. Unique for each call across the three tables Itemised Usage / Itemised Partial / Itemised Reject. Values directly from the Oracle sequence ITEMISED_USAGE_SEQ_NO (does not use the Unique Identifiers table).
ITEMISED_USAGE_NO_TEMP
Primary Keys
IU_NUMBER
Definition
Temporary table for use by the USAGE_LOADER process. Contains row numbers available for Itemised Usage records.
Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition
IU_NUMBER
NUMBER(20, 0)
N
A row UID to be used for an Itemised Usage record. Values directly from the Oracle sequence ITEMISED_USAGE_SEQ_NO (does not use the Unique Identifiers table).
ITEMISED_USAGE_SUCCESS_LOG
Primary Keys
IU_NUMBER
Definition
The USAGE_LOADER stores information about successful data processing here and uses it internally. The table identifies rows in the Itemised Usage / Partial /Reject tables that have been successfully processed.This table contains only transitory data, and does not require backup or archive.This is an Index Only table.
Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition

NUMBER(20, 0)
N
The row number (in the Itemised Usage, Itemised Partial, or Itemised Reject tables) which has been successfully processed.

LATE_PAYMENT_CHARGES
Primary Keys
Definition
Holds late payment charges generated when a bill is paid late. Note that there can be multiple rows per bill as (1) each payment can generate a separate LP charge and (2) a separate LP charge is raised for each different interest rate in force during the period over which interest is charged.
Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition
BILL_UID
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Identifies the bill on which this charge appears [Note - not the bill that was paid late, which is Orig Bill Uid]. Foreign key to Bill History
ORIG_BILL_UID
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Identifies the bill that was paid late and hence initiated generation of this charge. Foreign key to Bill History
ORIG_ASG_INVOICE_NO
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Only used if Account Sub Group invoice numbering is in use (system parameter ASGYN=Y), when it holds the account sub group invoice number. Defaults to 0.
ACCOUNT_SUB_GROUP_CD
VARCHAR2(5)
Y
Identifies the account sub group of the account for which this late payment charge was raised. Foreign key to Account Sub Group.
ORIG_BILL_TP_CD
CHAR(2)
N
Bill type of the bill that was paid late. List of possible values from Code where Code Tp Cd is 'BILL_TYPE'
ORIG_INVOICE_AMOUNT
FLOAT(126)
N
The original bill charge total plus credit total (credits are negative). Original bill means the bill that was paid late. Defaults to 0.
PAYMENT_AMOUNT
FLOAT(126)
N
Amount of payment included (NOT allocated) on the original bill. Original bill means the bill that was paid late. Defaults to 0.
BALANCE_AFTER_PAYMENT
FLOAT(126)
N
Orig Invoice Amount minus all previous payments minus allocated amount. Defaults to 0.
ALLOCATED_AMOUNT
FLOAT(126)
N
The allocated amount of the payment against the original bill for which the LPI charge is calculated. Note that a single payment can be allocated to two bills, and this column holds the amount allocated to the Orig Bill Uid only. Defaults to 0.
DUE_DATE
DATE
N
The Original Invoice Due Date plus Grace Period or the date when the start date of the late payment interest rate date (whatever is later).
PAYMENT_DATE
DATE
N
Date the payment was made which triggered generation of this LP charge. Where the interest rate has changed between the due date and the payment date, there will be two rows and the first will have this date set to the date of change of interest rate. Eg. due date = 1-Jan-2004, payment date = 1-Feb-2004, interest rate = 5% up to 15-Jan-2004, and 7% after. This table will have two rows, the first with Payment Date of 15-Jan-2004, the second with Payment Date of 1-Feb-2004
LPI_RATE
FLOAT(126)
N
The Late Payment Interest Rate used in calculation of this charge. Defaults to 0.
LPI_CHARGE
FLOAT(126)
N
The Late Payment Interest Charge (result of LPI Rate applied against the Allocated Amount). Defaults to 0.

LINEAR_ENTRY_TEXT
Primary Keys
ENTRY_UID,ALPHABETIC_YN,PART_CD,VERSION
Definition
Contains text entries for the telephone directory. Valid values are:1 - Person/Company Name2 - Additional text 13 - Address Line 14 - Street5 - Place Name6 - Area Name7 - Post Code8 - Additional text 29 - Access NumberThese have been added to the Codes table as codes of type DIRPARTCD.
Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition
ENTRY_UID
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Unique identifier for the entry. Values are taken from the unique identifier tables where Identifier_Tp_Cd = DIR_ALPHA. The primary key is on Entry_UID, Alphabetic_YN, Part_Cd, and Version, so a given entry can have both alphabetic and classified versions, different parts for each, and different versions for each part; only the most recent version for each part is used.
ALPHABETIC_YN
CHAR(1)
N
Indicates whether the entry is alphabetic (Y) or classified (N). There is no default value.
PART_CD
VARCHAR2(40)
N
Contains text entries for the telephone directory. Valid values are:1 - Person/Company Name2 - Additional text 13 - Address Line 14 - Street5 - Place Name6 - Area Name7 - Post Code8 - Additional text 29 - Access NumberThese have been added to the Codes table as codes of type DIRPARTCD.
VERSION
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Version of the entry. Later versions supersede earlier versions.
PART_VALUE
VARCHAR2(500)
Y
Text to be placed in the entry.
FONT_CD
VARCHAR2(10)
Y
Code defining the font, e.g. L (light, i.e. normal text), B (bold), SB (superbold), U (underlined). This, combined with an initial A for alphabetic or C for classified, is defined by the DIRFONTTAR code type in Codes.
TARIFF_VARIENT
VARCHAR2(100)
N
Indicates the tariff applicable to this row.Valid values are:(1) 'F' - free of charge(2) 'C' - the standard charge is applicable. This is ascertained from a string X, created by starting with an 'A' of Alphabetic or 'C' for Classified (depending on the value of Alphabetic_YN) and adding the value of Font_Cd. For example, if Alphabetic_YN = 'Y' and Font_Cd = 'L', then string X is 'AL'. This is then used to look up the tariff in Directory_Format_Tariff, where Code_Tp_Cd = 'DIRFONTTAR' and Code = string X. (3) A 'special' value, a tariff description which should correspond to Code_Des in Codes where Code_Tp_Cd = 'DIRFONTTAR'. The corresponding value of the Code column is then used to look up the appropriate tariff in the Directory_Format_Tariff table.

MASTER_ADDRESSES
Primary Keys
EXTERNAL_UID
Definition
This table holds a master list of addresses. The use is to provide a look-up of addresses exactly as held on an external system, so that addresses held on the Cerillion database can be linked directly to addresses held on an external system. This is achieved by the External UID which holds the UID on the external system. The value is written to the Addresses table whenever a Cerillion address is created by selecting from the Master Addresses table.Currently, the table is used for the N-Center line plant interface. It contains a list of addresses as held in N-Center, and is used to populate look up lists in Cerillion Front Office that are displayed whenever the user needs to create a new address. For example, the user can select an address from the list when creating a new servrce installation address. The External UID is recorded on the Addresses table. When the N-Center interface is invoked for the new service (access number), then the External UID is read from Addresses and passed to N-Center. In this way, both Cerillion and N-Center can be sure that they are referring to exactly the same address.This table is refreshed regularly from the external system database by a Cerillion batch process. This table includes the same columns as the Cerillion table Addresses, with the same uses. All fields must be populated exactly as required to be displayed on the Bills.

Only used in data migration process.Holds migrated payments that are not yet allocated to bills, and migrated credit bill amounts. MML_TEMPLATE_PLACEHOLDERS

Definition

Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition
MML_PLACEHOLDER_ID
VARCHAR2(50)
N
MML placeholder tag that may be used in MML_TEMPLATES text, e.g. "@email-header".
VALUE_TP_CD
VARCHAR2(10)
N
Defines how the value of placeholders is to be obtained. Values from Codes table where Code_Tp_Cd = 'MML_PLC_TP'. Currently, the values are: 'TAB' (placeholder is read from the Value column) 'SQL' (placeholder is obtained from the SQL query in the MML_Template_Placeholders_SQL table); 'SQLTVAL' (same as 'SQL', except that if no value is found in the other table, then the placeholder is obtained from the Value column). The default value for this column is 'SQL'.A table constraint enforces the rule that if Value_Tp_Cd = 'SQL', then Source_SQL_ID and Source_SQL_Column must be populated; if Value_Tp_Cd = 'VAL', then Value must be populated. If Source_SQL_ID is 'SQLTVAL', then there are no compulsory columns, although if neither Source_SQL_ID nor Value are populated, then obviously a template cannot be obtained.
VALUE
VARCHAR2(200)
Y
Default value of the placeholder. Must be populated if Value_Tp_Cd = 'VAL'.
SOURCE_SQL_ID
VARCHAR2(20)
Y
Reference of the SQL query which is to be used to get the placeholder value. Foreign key to MML_Template_Placeholders_SQL. Must be populated if Value_Tp_Cd is 'SQL'.
SOURCE_SQL_COLUMN
NUMBER(5, 0)
Y
Tells which data element (column) from the SQL query in MML_Template_Placeholders_SQL should be used as the placeholder value. This column is numeric, so for instance 3 would indicate that the third column in the SQL query should be used. Must be populated if Value_Tp_Cd is 'SQL'.

For most cases, the text or request to be sent to the target platform.Where the target platform is a REST web service, the value is constructed from the following fields, in the specified order, separated by a delimiter that consists of the all characters at the beginning of the value up to but not including the 1st "!" character (optional fields, depicted below by [], must be specified as empty values, i.e. 2 consecutive delimiters):"HTTP method - GET, PUT, PATCH, POST, DELETE"[Flag to indicate whether to follow redirects (default to false)]"[Endpoint completion (contains anything valid in a URL, apart from…)]"[Query string (contains &, "alphabetic", decimal digits, %)]"[Content type if there's a message body. Do not include charset - if included, it will be ignored as we currently UTF-8 encode the content and supply the charset element of the content type; we may need to be more flexible in the future and allow any charset and convert charset name to Java charset name, but that's potentially problematic as the set of acceptable charset names for the HTTP Content-Type header is different from the set of charset names supported by Java, so we may not want to take that route.]"[Content (message body - only really relevant for certain HTTP methods, e.g. PUT/PATCH/POST, but allow for all)]"Accept type for response"[Message type for MML decodes to obtain fields from response]"[Any number of request properties (HTTP headers) expressed as name/value pairs, separated by the delimiter, with name and value in each pair separated by an = character]An example value for a GET REST operation with no content type and no content is:(delim)!GET(delim)true(delim)weather(delim)lat=35&lon=139&appid=b6907d289e10d714a6e88b30761fae22(delim)(delim)(delim)application/json(delim)getweatherand another example including request properties:(delim)!GET(delim)true(delim)weather(delim)lat=35&lon=139&appid=b6907d289e10d714a6e88b30761fae22(delim)(delim)(delim)application/json(delim)getweather(delim)user=ethelred(delim)password=unread

NETWORK
Primary Keys
NETWORK_CODE,EXCHANGE_TP_CD
Definition
Holds detail about the different networks to which Cerillion interfaces via the provisioning sub-system.There can be several networks, each identified by a unique code, and each network can have multiple types of connection. For example, a fixed wire network may have two types of exchanges which are separately connected to Cerillion.There is only one connection of each type to each network  - hence the primary key definition.
