NETWORK_SVC_NODE
Primary Keys
FUNCTION_CODE,NETWORK_SERVICE_CD
Definition
Lists the nodes that make up the definition of network services, the page on which they are available and presentation order. This represents nodes of a tree consisting of a network service (at the top level) and actions (at subsequent levels). Note that a top level network service may also have actions defined against it. Eg for voicemail:Voicemail [Provide] [De-Provide]      Change Language [Choose Language]In this example, this table has 2 rows - One for Voicemail, on for Change Language. The Parent Service Cd of Change Language, will be Voicemail.The actions available to each node are described in Network Svc Prov Action - actions available for a given Network Service. For example, for the Voicemail  network service, available actions may be Provide, De-provide, Change PIN etc
Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition

N
Identifies the function (ie the CRM page) on which this network action will be available

TREE_LEVEL
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Defines the level of the node in the tree 0 = the highest level, 1  = the next down; no other values are valid.
PRESENTATION_ORDER
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Defines the order in which the actions are presented to the user. This is only within a top level node and it's sub nodes, and not down the whole tree.

For second level nodes (tree_level = 1), links to the parent node. Is set to NULL for top level nodes (tree_level = 0). Foreign key to this table.

NOTEPADS
Primary Keys
Definition
A general note area. Any text can be recorded hereThe logical primary key is Notepad UID and Line No, but to simplify the data model, the Notepad UID is used as the primary key (plus Note Tp Cd, as for PRION and PRIOF note types, the same notepad uid is is used).Note that the key structure causes problems in defining relationships for this table. In other tables the Notepad UID is used as a foreign key, even though it is non-unique in this table. The data model shows a 1:1 relationship between Note pads and the other tables, but really it is a 1-to-many, many notepads with same uid (but different line numbers) for one of the other tables.

ORIGIN_GROUPS
Primary Keys
ORIGIN_GROUP_UID
Definition
Defines groupings of Origins. These allow multiple Origins to use a single Connection. This can dramatically reduce the number of Connections required. (e.g. all UK origins may have the same charges to the US, but require different configuration for domestic use. With Origin Groups only one set of links is required to the US instead of one per UK area code).

PAGE_CONFIGURATION_CROSS_VAL
Primary Keys
PAGE_NAME,FORM_NAME,TRIGGER_FIELD_NAME,TRIGGER_OPERATOR_CD,TRIGGER_FIELD_VALUE,RECEIVER_FIELD_NAME
Definition
Stores cross field validation for configurable forms defined in PAGE_CONFIGURATION and PAGE_CONFIGURATION_FIELD.Validation is applied to the RECEIVER_FIELD if the TRIGGER_FIELD meets the given condition. Validation applied on the RECEIVER_FIELD is, for example, changing the dropdown list, or changing the REGEX pattern validation.For example, if field A (TARGET_FIELD) provides a list of identification numbers (passport no, drivers license no, ...), and field B (RECEIVER_FIELD) allows you to enter the value, then field B can conditionally change its REGEX pattern validation to match the selected id type in field A.Or if field A (TARGET_FIELD) provides a list of identification types, and field B (RECEIVER_FIELD) allows you to choose the issuing country, then field B can conditionally change its drop down list to show valid issuing countries for the selected id type in field A.

The description showed on display unit when doing a refund. It is mandatory, if the EPOS Display Code is different from NONE.Used in POS0102S to set the display text.
CARD_SCHEME
VARCHAR2(10)
Y
Shortened identifier of a card type, e.g. AMEX, DINERS, MASTERS, etc. Used for some strange reason in EPOS instead the Payment Code (but only sometimes). It is mandatory if the Credit Card YN column is set to Y. It must match the card scheme recognised by any credit card server in use, that use card schemes - currentl WinEFT only. (Refer to credit card server documentation for allowed values)This field is used in the Credit Card screen (POS0123S) to set the scheme based on the payment code selected by the user in the Enter Amount screen (POS0112S).Also used in POS0123S to set the payment types based upon the scheme returned from the EFT function module POS0102S07 [WinEFT only].This field is also used in EFT functions module POS0102S07 to set the scheme based upon the Server Card Scheme returned from the credit card server.
CARD_SCHEME_TEXT
VARCHAR2(10)
Y
Shortened text description of a card type, e.g. "Master". It is used to display information to the user. such as "Swipe Mastercard. It is mandatory, if the Credit Card YN column is set to Y.This and the Card Scheme column contain the same information, but Card Scheme values must match those used by the credit card server (currently for WinEFT only), whereas this fields can have any text as required by the Operator for display to the user.
SERVER_CARD_SCHEME
VARCHAR2(40)
Y
A full textual description of the scheme, e.g. "American Express" or "MasterCard". It is returned by the Credit card Server (currently for WinEFT only) and used by EPOS to find the Card Scheme that the server thinks has been used. It is mandatory, if the Credit Card YN column is set to Y.This field is used in EFT function module POS0102S07 to search the scheme text returned from the Credit Card Server. When a match is found the scheme is set to the Card Scheme column value.The field can contain a comma seperated list of schemes.

Definition
Provides a work order profile for the sale of a product or package. This table has been amended for CPC-1419 (Sales Manager Phase II).All searches are within METHOD_CD. Two searches are performed, one at DEFN_LEVEL_CD = 'I'. If a match is found then the list of work order profiles are taken from PRODUCT_WORK_ORDER_PROF_LIST following the PROFILE_LIST_UID. Failing a match then a second search is performed at DEFN_LEVEL_CD = 'G'. ·The work_order_tariff_groups table is not used at all by the New Sales Manager.

Some provisioning drivers process files of responses.  If processing is halted midway through a file the driver must be able to recommence processing from where it stopped.  This table holds the last processed record number for a file so the driver may start again.

PROV_DRIVER_FILE_LOCKED_SESSNS
Primary Keys
DRIVER_TYPE_CD,NETWORK_CODE,FILENAME,KNOWLEDGE_SESSION_UID
Definition
Provisioning drivers that process files of responses must notify  knowledge sessions of each reponse.  Sometime thay will find the knowledge session they require is licked (because it is busy processing another request/response).  Under these circumstances the driver will record the uid of the locked session in this table and will  mark the response as unprocessed, it will not attempt to process any further response in the file that is intended for the same knowledge session.These drivers use a database table for this purpose, rather than in-process memory, to facilitate recommencing after a shutdown.
Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition
DRIVER_TYPE_CD
VARCHAR2(10)
N
List of possible values from Codes where Code Tp Cd is 'PROVDRIVER'
NETWORK_CODE
VARCHAR2(5)
N
From network table
FILENAME
VARCHAR2(256)
N
The name of the file being processed.
KNOWLEDGE_SESSION_UID
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
The uid of the locked session.

CHAR(1)
N
Some errors can be fixed, for example, for CPS, by getting the correct post code from a subscriber, these errors should have have this field set to 'Y', the response handling logic uses this field to determine whether to create a work order to fix the problem and resubmit the request or to simply set the provision to a failed status. Default is N.

PUK_DETAILS
Primary Keys
ICCID
Definition
Defines the available GSM identities that can be used in the GSM switch. On a simple level is a mapping from the ICCID number (available to everyone) and the IMSI number (private, used internally when making call). One row in this table equates to one SIM card - although this table is not intended to be the definition of a SIM card.  The rows are created from batch update processes, and then available for selection when a new GSM service is provided.  The table represents two types of ICCIDS (SIM cards) - paired and unpaired. Paired SIM cards are those where the card is paired with an MSISDN (access number) before allocation to a new service. Unpaired SIM cards are those where there is no MSISDN allocated until sales time, when the SIM card and access number are allocated to the service separately.
Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition
ICCID
VARCHAR2(40)
N
The ICCID.NOTE - this field is 40 characters but should not be - only the first 13 are ever populated.

CHAR(4)
N
The Personal Identification Number (PIN). Defaults to ' '.

VARCHAR2(256)
Y
MSISDN paired with the ICCID. Set to NULL for unpaired SIM cards. Excludes the country code. (e.g. 44 for UK, 299 for Greenland etc)** NOTE - Only used where SIM Cards are paired with Access Numbers prior to sale **
DEALER_CD
VARCHAR2(4)
Y
Dealer to whom the ICCID has been allocated. Will be NULL is not allocated to a dealer. List of possible values in Codes table, where Code Type is 'DEALER'
STATUS_CD
CHAR(2)
N
Status of the ICCID. Possible values are:AD - Allocated to Dealer (The Dealer can sell to Subscriber)AS - Allocated to subscriber UA - Unallocated/ Available for saleLP - Loaded and waiting to be packed (not available to sell)LS - Loaded and sent for packing (not available to sell)** NOTE - Only used where SIM Cards are paired with Access Numbers prior to sale **

RELATION_DEFINITION
Primary Keys
RELATION_DEFINITION_UID
Definition
Defines system type relationships (system_fixed_yn=Y), providing the links between customers and accounts (ACCOUNTOF) and parent child relationships between accounts. For the latter, there are two types of link: CHILDOF for the Hierarchies functionality, and PAYSFOR for roll-up billing. System relationships may also have one or more categories, defined in the Relation Category table.The Relation Definition table may also define the types of peer-to-peer relations used within Cerillion CRM (system_fixed_yn=N).  A relation definition must be in force for a relation to be created. This type of relation is for information only.*** The data in this table is defined by the RelationDefinition.xls spreadsheet in the Data Model. ***

Reason for the relation. List of possible value from Codes where  Code Tp Cd  is RELA_REAS

REMOTE_SESSION_LOG
Primary Keys
Definition
Holds a log of user access to Cerillion via the Front Office GUI. A row is inserted every time a user logs on or logs off Cerillion. No row will be written if the user reboots their PC whilst logged in to Cerillion.There is no functionality at present to read from the table.The table is populated by the trigger CERI_LOGON, and can become very large, causing some performance problems. The trigger has therefore been officially dropped from the Data Model (see CER-22052) and the table may be regarded as being redundant, although the CERI_LOGON trigger may continue to exist on some Cerillion databases.If users require, they can retain the CERI_LOGON trigger in order to be able to check the information on Cerillin logins held in this table. However, it will be the users' responsibility to regularly archive and/or delete older records, to prevent the table becoming too large.
Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition
INGRES_USERNAME
VARCHAR2(5)
N
User name of person currently logged on - links to same column on Staff table.
LOG_DT
DATE
N
Date and time of the log on or log off event.
LOG_SESSION_ACTION_CD
VARCHAR2(5)
N
Code which indicates the logged event-will be a code for either log on (ORLON) or log off (ORLOF)
LOG_SESSION_ACTION_LINE_NO
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
A sequence number to allow more than one row to be written per event.  This is used to store more details of the event in multiple rows using the Log Session Info.  The sequence number starts at 0 (the default value). Currently not used
LOG_SESSION_INFO
VARCHAR2(200)
N
Text information about the event-e.g. the version of software being run when logging on to Cerillion

RTM_ORDER
Primary Keys
RTM_ORDER_UID
Definition
Contains details of a single order from an RTM File.After the file has been file-level validated (not zero-length, valid XML, contains orders), the order-XML is placed in the Source XML column. Status is updated as operations fail/succeed on this record, once status is final, record is stale and can be purged.If the RTM functionality is being used, and the XML is being stored here, then the following function-baased indexes are required. These provide indexes onto elements within the XML data held in Source_XML.CREATE INDEX I_RO_FUNC_CLI_INDEXON RTM_ORDER RO (                SUBSTR(sys.XMLTYPE.getStringVal(sys.XMLTYPE.EXTRACT                (RO.SOURCE_XML,'//CLI')),1,40))LOGGINGTABLESPACE DATA01PCTFREE    10INITRANS   2MAXTRANS   255STORAGE    (            INITIAL          1M            NEXT             1M            MINEXTENTS       1            MAXEXTENTS       2147483645            PCTINCREASE      0            BUFFER_POOL      DEFAULT           )NOPARALLEL/CREATE INDEX I_RO_FUNC_ORDER_COMPANY ON RTM_ORDER RO (                SUBSTR(sys.XMLTYPE.getStringVal(sys.XMLTYPE.EXTRACT                (RO.SOURCE_XML,'/NewBusinessOrder/CustomerDetails/CompanyName')),1,40))LOGGINGTABLESPACE DATA01PCTFREE    10INITRANS   2MAXTRANS   255STORAGE    (            INITIAL          1M            NEXT             1M            MINEXTENTS       1            MAXEXTENTS       2147483645            PCTINCREASE      0            BUFFER_POOL      DEFAULT           )NOPARALLEL/CREATE INDEX I_RO_FUNC_SURNAME ON RTM_ORDER RO (                SUBSTR(sys.XMLTYPE.getStringVal(sys.XMLTYPE.EXTRACT                (RO.SOURCE_XML,'//LastName')),1,40))LOGGINGTABLESPACE DATA01PCTFREE    10INITRANS   2MAXTRANS   255STORAGE    (            INITIAL          1M            NEXT             1M            MINEXTENTS       1            MAXEXTENTS       2147483645            PCTINCREASE      0            BUFFER_POOL      DEFAULT           )NOPARALLEL/

RULE_NAME,RTM_CLIENT_UID
Definition
Validation rules are applied on a per-RTM basis. For each applicable rule an RTM can either:1. have rule NOT APPLYor2. On validation failure:    · Have error moved to INTERNAL quarantine     · Have record moved to EXTERNAL quarantine     · Continue processing. 
Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition
RULE_NAME
VARCHAR2(30)
N
Idenifies the rule, foreign key to RTMLoader Validation Rule
RTM_CLIENT_UID
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Defines the client for which the action is defined when this rule is applied.
RULE_ACTION
VARCHAR2(20)
N
Action to taken when the rule is applied to the RTM. Foreign key to RTMLoader Rule Action

Maps error descriptions to error codes and indicate the stage / reason why a file / order has failed RTM Load validation. A summary of these codes will be placed in the RTM return error file. *** The data in this table is defined by the RTMConfig.xls spreadsheet in the Data Model. ***

SCHEDULED_FOR_WRITE_OFF
Primary Keys
PRIME_UID
Definition
Holds all accounts which have been selected for write off. Currently the Final Bill Generation process inserts records into this table but any process can insert records in this table. The write-off process,  will look at this table and carry out the write-off of all the accounts in the table. The write-off process will not carry any further validations on the selected accounts. The idea is that the insertion of records into the table is done based on criterias which vary from process to process, and the write-off process is a generic module that simply writes off the accounts which are in the table.

SEGMENTATION_METHOD
Primary Keys
METHOD_UID
Definition
The table holds details of how to derive the value that drives product segmentation. Each rule in PRODUCT_SEGMENTATION_RULE references a row in this table.
Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition
METHOD_UID
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Primary key – uid of type PRDSEGMTHD.
METHOD_TYPE
VARCHAR2(50)
N
One of ACCOUNT_NO, ADDRESS_NODE, ADDRESS_UID, EQUIP_UID (post-sales only), EXTERNAL_SYSTEM, SQL_QUERY and USERNAME.Foreign key to PRODUCT_SEGMENTATION_MTHD_TYPE table.
LOOKUP_TABLE
VARCHAR2(128)
Y
The table to get the segmentation value from – only applicable when METHOD_TYPE is one of ACCOUNT_NO, ADDRESS_UID, EQUIP_UID and USERNAME.
LOOKUP_KEY_COLUMN
VARCHAR2(128)
Y
The name of the column in the table specified by LOOKUP_TABLE that uniquely identifies a row (normally the primary key column) – only applicable when METHOD_TYPE one of ACCOUNT_NO, ADDRESS_UID, EQUIP_UID and USERNAME.
LOOKUP_VALUE_COLUMN
VARCHAR2(128)
Y
The name of the column in in the table specified by LOOKUP_TABLE from which to get the segmentation value – only applicable when METHOD_TYPE one of ACCOUNT_NO, ADDRESS_UID, EQUIP_UID and USERNAME. The value specified must be of type CHAR or VARCHAR2, so, for example, a NUMBER column ABC would need to be specified as TO_CHAR(ABC).
METHOD_DESCRIPTION
VARCHAR2(4000)
N
Description of method
SQL_QUERY
CLOB
Y
The SQL query to use when METHOD_TYPE is SQL_QUERY. The query must result in a single value that can be mapped to one or more tariff groups using PRODUCT_SEGMENTATION_RULE. The query can contain ":accountNo", ":addressUid", ":equipUid", or ":username" as a substitution parameter, in which case the system provides the value of that parameter based on the current sale context. Note that the query result must be of type CHAR or VARCHAR2.
SEGMENTATION_RULE
Primary Keys
RULE_UID
Definition
Defines the mapping from different types of value or value range to sets of product groups (tariff groups), where a set may consist of one or more items. The types of value/range depend on the corresponding method in PRODUCT_SEGMENTATION_METHOD, as identified by METHOD_UID.
Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition
RULE_UID
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Primary key – uid of type PRDSEGRULE.
GROUP_UID
NUMBER(11, 0)
Y
Uid of type PRDSEGRLGP.
METHOD_UID
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Foreign key to PRODUCT_SEGMENTATION_METHOD table.
RANGE_START
VARCHAR2(4000)
Y
The start of the range of values that satisfy this rule (if null, but RANGE_END is not null, there is no lower limit)
RANGE_END
VARCHAR2(4000)
Y
The end of the range of values that satisfy this rule (if null, but RANGE_START is not null, there is no upper limit)
MAPPED_VALUE
VARCHAR2(4000)
Y
A value of type defined by the method identified by METHOD_UID, which maps to a set of tariff groups in PRODUCT_SEGMENTATION_RULE_ITEM, identified by RULE_UID. The value can include standard SQL wildcard characters (% and _), in which case the match condition is LIKE MAPPED_VALUE rather than = MAPPED_VALUE. If MAPPED_VALUE needs to contain literal % or _ characters, precede each one with the ‘\’ character, for example ‘ABC\_%\_XYZ’ to match any value that begins with “ABC_ and ends with “_XYZ”.
NEGATE_MAPPING_YN
CHAR(1)
N
Flag to indicate whether to invert the mapping to its opposite meaning, so that:• for a plain MAPPED_VALUE, the mapping means “!= MAPPED_VALUE”• for wildcarded MAPPED_VALUE, the mapping means “NOT LIKE MAPPED_VALUE”• for a range, the mapping means “NOT BETWEEN RANGE_START AND RANGE_END”
DESCRIPTION
VARCHAR2(4000)
N
SOFT_RULE_YN
CHAR(1)
N
If set to 'Y' then rule will be considered as soft rule.
SOFT_CHECK_WARNING
VARCHAR2(255)
Y
Warning message to be displayed when soft rule failed.

SERVICE_CONTINUATION
Primary Keys
SERVICE_UID,SEQ_NO
Definition
This table records the sequence of Access Number or Equipment instancess that comprise a single continuous service.An entry is added to this table by work order completion for each Access Number and Equipment on a successfully completed 'provide' work order.For a stand-alone provide work order, or provide order that is one half of a non-continuation of service composite work order:  - A new Service UID will be created for each Access Number and Equipment on the work order, and Seq No will be set to 1.Fora  provide work order that is one half of a continuation of service composite work order:  - Each Access Number and Equipment on the work order that continues a previous entry will be assigned the same Service UID and Seq No incremented by one.  - Each Access Number and Equipment that does not continue a previous entry is assigned a new Service UID and Seq No will be set to 1.
Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition
SERVICE_UID
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Unique identifier for a continuous service.  Taken from the SERVICE uid  range.Note - unlike other UIDs, not the primary key of a table as a single service instance can have multiple rows with the same UID. Part of primary key with Seq No.
SEQ_NO
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Sequence number starting from 1, and incremented each time a continuation of service change creates a new entry in Access Numbers or Equipment for a given Service UID.Part of primary key with Service UID.
EQUIP_UID
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Identifies the Access Numbers or Equipment instance that formes this service.Pseudo foreign key to entry in either Access Numbers or Equipment.
WO_NO
NUMBER(11, 0)
Y
Unique id for this record.  Taken from the WORK ORDER uid  range.

Definition
Stores all single credit card transaction details. Added for CPC-1010.CPC-1214: A payment can be at different stages and each stage can be successful or fail.For example:Stage of AUTH and Status of SUCCESS means that the authorisation of the payment was completed and it was successful.Stage of AUTH and Status of FAILURE means that the authorisation of the payment was completed and it was not successful.Stage of PROC and Status of SUCCESS means that the successfully authorised payment was posted into Cerillion and it was successful.Stage of PROC and Status of FAILURE means that the successfully authorised payment was posted into Cerillion, but the posting failed.The REQ stage of the payment will not have any status associated with it.

SITE_EVENT_DEFN
Primary Keys
EVENT_TYPE_CD,EVENT_SUB_TYPE_CD
Definition
Defines events specific to a site. These are site defined and created, and can be changed directly or via the Administrator. Together with System Event Defn, this table supersedes Cerillion Event Defn under CPC-1119. Cerillion Event Defn is now a view based on a union of both new tables. Site Event Defn contains all the columns found in System Event defn, apart from Standalone Event YN and Can CSR Create YN (because all site-defined events are standalone and can be created by the user). Any new columns added to System Event Defn should also be added to Site Event Defn, and the Cerillion Event Defn view.

NUMBER(3, 0)
Y
Indicates the number of months of data (backwards from the current date) that cannot be archived by the Events Archiver process. This should be configured to a value greater than or equal to the minimum event archive cutoff months (MINIMUM_CUT_OFF_MONTHS in the Process Defaults table). If the Exempt From Archiving YN column is null, then the cutoff used is that held for CUT_OFF_MONTHS in Process Defaults. If Exempt From Archiving YN is below the MINIMUM_CUT_OFF_MONTHS value in Process Defaults, then the latter value overrides the value in this column. Added for CPC-1168.

STAFF
Primary Keys
INGRES_USERNAME
Definition
A list of the staff who are able to use the Cerillion system. The primary key is on Ingres_Username, a 5-character code, but it was formerly on the numeric Staff_No, and uniqueness is still enforced on the latter field. The Staff_Level_Cd and Staff_Group_Cd determine where in the account group/account sub group hierarchy this member of staff works. Possible combinations are:  1. User works at top level (level Cd = HQ, group Cd = null) 2. User works at account group level (level Cd = AG. group Cd = account group code) 3. User works at account sub group level (level Cd = ASG, group Cd = account sub group code)
Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null

CHAR(5)
N
A 5 letter alphanumeric string beginning with a letter, used by the user for logging into the system and also to record the user's identity within Cerillion (It is recommended that the same id is used as the user's network id to control access to the PC network.)

SUBSCRIBERS
Primary Keys
ACCOUNT_NO
Definition
Holds details about each account holder. The terms 'account' and 'subscriber' can be used interchangeably.This is not to be confused with the Customers table, which represents individual customers. A single customer could have multiple accounts (for example, a residential account and a business account), represented by rows in the Subscribers table.Note: from CDM19 / Cerillion 2_1_00 onwards, relations between subscribers and customers, previously represented by the customer_uid column, are now defined by rows in the Relation_Instance table.Similarly, hierarchical relations between subscribers, previously represented by the parent_account_no column, are also defined by rows in the Relation_Instance table.The upgrade script 18_to_19_insert_relations.sql converts data in the customer_uid and parent_account_no columns, into rows in the Relation_Definition table.The customer_uid and parent_account_no columns are dropped altogether in CDM28 and the Product Kernel and all Data Models based on it.Further information on the Intranet page: http://intranet/display/DEV/Relations .

ACCOUNT_CLASS_CD
CHAR(2)
Y
A method for classifying accounts. This can be configured to be anything required, as the list of categories is held in Codes with Code Type = 'ACCOUNT' and code category 'CO'. However, it is used by Bill_Cycle_Control to determine the allocation of accounts to bill cycles. The WHSLE system parameter determines which account class codes refer to wholesale accounts. The terms 'Account class' and 'account type' are generally used interchangeably in the system.
ACC_CATEGORY_CD
CHAR(2)
Y
An alternative method for classifying accounts. This can also be configured to be anything required, as the list of categories is held in Codes with Code Type = 'CATEGORY' and code category 'CO'. The field is used by the Wholesale_Cat_Map table to map account categories to wholesale account numbers, and by the IEACC system parameter to determine which account categories are included in the Itemised Usage export process.

STATUS_CD
CHAR(2)
N
List of possible options in Codes with Code Type = 'SUBSCRIBER'.  Accounts currently being billed cyclically are in status SN (Subscriber Normal).  This status changes to SF (Subscriber Final) upon final billing, after which the only charges that can be ledgered against it are late usage charges.  SW (Subscriber Written off) means that the outstanding charges on the account has been written off-: the subscriber may have an outstanding balance, but there will be no further attempt made to reclaim money owed and no more bills will be generated.  SW changes to SR (Subscriber Reactivated) if the subscriber account is re-activates

NUMBER(3, 0)
Y
Indicates the number of months of data (backwards from the current date) that cannot be archived by the Events Archiver process. This should be configured to a value greater than or equal to the minimum event archive cutoff months (MINIMUM_CUT_OFF_MONTHS in the Process Defaults table). If the Exempt From Archiving YN column is null, then the cutoff used is that held for CUT_OFF_MONTHS in Process Defaults. If Exempt From Archiving YN is below the MINIMUM_CUT_OFF_MONTHS value in Process Defaults, then the latter value overrides the value in this column. Added for CPC-1168.

Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition
TARIFF_CODE
VARCHAR2(8)
N
Foreign key to TARIFF_HEADERS
BAL_EXPIRY_EXPRESSION
VARCHAR2(100)
Y
It can be configured for non recurring balances. Simple SQL expressions can be configured to derive balance expiry date and time. Only allowed bind variable currently is :fromDt.     Examples    Examples:1. if set to :fromDt + 12/24, balance will be valid for 12 hours.2. if set it to trunc( :fromDt - 6/24)+1+6/24,  if balance start time is between midnight (00:00:00) and 05:59:59, it'll end at 6 AM of same day else will end at 6 AM of next day.         In  simple terms, configured SQL expression should be such that 'select :expression from dual' should return a valid date.                                                                                         If we want balance to expire on a particular date and time, it can be specified in format 'YYYY_MM_DD HH24:MI:SS' OR 'YYYY_MM_DD', for e.g. if set to '2023:12:25', balance will expire at Christmas midnight, i.e. 25-Dec-2023 00:00:00
BAL_EXPIRY_TIME
VARCHAR2(8)
Y
It must be configured in format HH24:MI:SS. It can be configured for recurring (daily / weekly only) / non recurring balance. If configured, it'll override the time part of balance expiry date. If not set, balance expiry date / time will follow perfect anniversary (unless balance_override_expression is set). For e.g. a daily recurring balance will expire after 24 hours. It can be used to expire balances at a particular time, for e.g. midnight by setting it to 23:59:59. This field works in conjuction with bal_expiry_days, bal_expiry_expression and will override the time part of balance expiry.

BALANCE_OVERRIDE_EXPRESSION
VARCHAR2(50)
Y
This specifies a simple mathematical expression to specify monetary / non monetary balance value in terms of payment amount. It supports only two bind variables :paymentAmount, :initialValue, where :initialValue would be considered as combination of bal_initial_amount_digits, bal_initial_amount_exp. For e.g. for monetary balance, it could be configured as :paymentAmount, which means a $12.52 top up would top up monetary balance by $12.52. If it's configured as (:initialValue/ :paymentAmount)*1.5, where bal_initial_amount_value is defined as 1000, bal_initial_amount_exp is -1 and one does a top up of $12, corresponding balance value topped up would be (100/12)*1.5 = 12.5. For non monetary balances, result would be rounded to nearest integer value.
SALE_THRESHOLD_TARIFF_CODE

Y

The action for each threshold is defined in columns BALANCE_THRESHOLD_DEFN.*_THRESHOLD_ACTION_TP_CD

Definition
Holds discounts that can apply to periodic  or one off tariff charges. For discounts on periodic charges the following apply:-          The discount  can only be a percentage discount-          Only one of the filters on Account Class Code, Account Number and Discount Group Code can be used for each discount definition. Combinations of filters are not supported. For discounts on non-periodic charges given on account sales the following apply:-          The discount  can only be a percentage discount-          Only one of following filters can be used for each discount definition. All other combinations are not supportedo   Account Number and Discount Groupo   Account Numbero   Account Class For discounts on non-periodic changes given on non-account sales the following apply:-          The discount  can be a percentage discount or flat rate amount-          All of Account Number, Account Class and Discount Group must be NULL for the discount to be applied

Defines penalties attached to a tariff charge. Penalties are applied on early termination of a service, and choice of penalty depends on the time between service start and service termination.Note that more than one penalty can apply to a single tariff charge.
Columns

Datatype
Null

N
Version of the tariff charge for which the penaly applies.Combination of Tariff Code, Sx and Version are foreign key to Tariff Suffix Versions, and define the charge for which a penalty will be applied if the service to which the charge relates is terminated early. Generally this wll be a rental charge to support the raising of a penalty if a fixed term contract is terminated early.
PENALTY_MONTH_LIMIT
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
The number of whole months, from start of service, during which a penalty can occur.Termination of service, within this period, will trigger the penalty. Period is not inclusive, i.e. test is "number of months LESS THAN Penalty Month Limit".Example. A value of 3 means a T.O.S. less than (but not including) 3 calendar months from service start, will receive the penalty

OBSOLETE_YN
CHAR(1)
N
This flag is used to set whether a tariff is obsolete or not.  If it is, then nobody is being charged using this version.  A version of a connection charge becomes obsolete as soon as the version is superseded, but a version of the rental charge can only become obsolete when everyone who was paying rental on that tariff has been moved to pay rental on a different version. Default is N.

N
If this is 'Y' then the CSR is allowed to amend the charge for this tariff when adding it to a work order.  When the charge is amended a one-off version of the tariff is created in this table where Special Ver YN = 'Y' and Sales Amend YN = 'N', and this version is labelled with the work order number for the work order that this special version was created for.

TRANSACTION_CODES
Primary Keys
CODE
Definition
Defines a transaction type - for example, rental charge, connection charge, sales volume discount, invoice payment etc. These are widely used in financial tables and therefore the transaction_codes table has many child tables, including accounts_receivable, usage_tariffs, billed/unbilled_ciu_summary. The table also contains information required for financial reporting purposes.*** The data in this table is defined by the TransactionCodes.xls spreadsheet in the Data Model. ***
Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition
CODE
VARCHAR2(6)
N
The transaction code; primary key. The first two letters normally follow the following convention: CH: charge; CR: credit; PY: payment; RV: reversal. Less widely used prefixes are: CI: invisible credit; DB: debit; RC: credit refund; RF: refer to drawer; TR: till roll transaction; CP: prior period; CD: dispute. 
CODE_DES
VARCHAR2(25)
N
Free text description of the transaction code.
REVERSE_TRANS_CODE
VARCHAR2(6)
Y
The transaction code used to reverse a transaction of this type. This should always have the prefix RV. This field is a recursive foreign key to the Code column in this table, therefore all the reversal transaction codes should also have a row of their own. This field is nullable and should obviously be blank for reversal transaction code rows, but should be populated for all other rows.Note that a reversal is not the same as a credit.

If the transaction code begins with CR or CI, then the value must be 'YES' or 'NO'. 2. A pre-insert/update trigger enforces the above logic.

USAGE_TARIFFS
Primary Keys
TARIFF_CODE_UID
Definition
Defines the usage tariff instances.  It is important to note that there are two totally separate methods of accessing this table:1. 'old usage tariffs' that define the original group and metered usage charges.  The key being directly via the tariff_headers table.2. 'new usage tariffs' that define the itemised usage tariff charges.  The key being via the gsm tariff groups table & indirectly from the tariff headers table by virtue of the usage_tp_cdThe column names are very confusing. Tariff Code and Tariff Ver refers to Tariff Group Code and Tariff Ver in the GSM Tariff Group Codes table. Tariff Group Code is a code for grouping of tariffs. TAKE CARE WITH THIS!This table holds each version of the data.  Only the latest revision is held for each version.  It is in essence the core table from which the rest of the system retrieves its data. (see also the usage_tariff_history, usage_tariffs_wip, usage_tariff_revisions and usage_tariffs_revision_history)

TOLL_CHARGE_YN
CHAR(1)
Y
'Y' indicates thate this tariff has an additional toll element, defined by the fields prefixed with toll_.Any other value (including null) indicates that the toll_ fields should be ignored/not filled in, and that there is no toll element to this tariff."Toll" is a USA term for the charge for the long distance element of the call. The local element is defined by the rest of the tariff definition. This means a call rated using this tariff has two separate charges - one for local and one for toll.

USAGE_TARIFFS_LOOKUP
Primary Keys
Definition
Gives a simplified version of the usage tariffs.  It can be used by external systems to populate the display of tariffs  - eg in a web application to online users.Cerillion populates this table from the current tariffs within the system. This table holds usage tariffs for voice, fax, data, SMS, content, supplementary services and also roaming charges for receiving a call whilst on another operators network.   Roaming charges for making a call whilst on another operators network are not included.Data detailing the discounts that apply to the tariffs is also supplied within the table.  Where a tariff has multiple corresponding discounts the details for the discount with the highest discount priority are given. ·This table will be populated primarily by data taken from the following database tables - usage_tariffs, connections and destinations.  The description fields will be populated from many tables including codes, gsm_distance_bands, itemisation_destinations, timeplans, timeslots, event_sources, event_actions and event_types.No indexes or keys are given. Indexing must be performed according to the method employed in extracting data, which will vary from site to site.

USAGE_TARIFFS_PENDING_ACTIVATE
Primary Keys
TARIFF_ACTIVATE_UID
Definition
Holds the activation information for the usage tariffs, this being  a stage between WIP and Active - called Pending. The activation information is inserted between the WIP and Pending sections. This information has to be stored, so that when the tariff is activated from pending, the details can be used in the activation process.

USAGE_TARIFFS_REVISION_HISTORY
Primary Keys
SERVICE_CD,USAGE_TP_CD,TARIFF_TP_CD,TARIFF_VER,TARIFF_REV
Definition
This table holds a description plus additional information for any changes that are activated as a new version or revision to an existing version.  It can be seen to be a history of changes to the revisions table.The table stores details relating to the date the version was created, who created it, a key to the description of the change, and key field(s) that identify the version within the core table (usage_tariffs)

'Y' indicates thate this tariff has an additional toll element, defined by the fields prefixed with toll_.Any other value (including null) indicates that the toll_ fields should be ignored/not filled in, and that there is no toll element to this tariff."Toll" is a USA term for the charge for the long distance element of the call. The local element is defined by the rest of the tariff definition. This means a call rated using this tariff has two separate charges - one for local and one for toll.

Holds a mapping from a BT WLR Select Sevice and option, to the Cerillion product that represents it.The option is set to 'YES' for most select services which only a yes/no option - yes being indicated by the presence of the tariff against the WLR servuice, and no by it's absenceWhere a select service can have multiple options, then a distinct Cerillion tariff must be configured for each. For example, if the select service has options, yes/no/gold, then there will be two tariffs one for yes, one for gold.

Primary Keys
RULE_UID
Definition
It contains the definition of decision rules used to determine if and when a work order step activates: each rule results into the generation/ capture of a single value.  The type of value and how it is retrieved or captured are all attributes defined in the rule.
Columns 
Column Name
Datatype
Null
Definition
RULE_UID
NUMBER(11, 0)
N
Primary key. Unique identifier type is WOPRULEUID.
RULE_NAME
VARCHAR2(200)
N
Rule name. 
RULE_TYPE_CD
VARCHAR2(10)
N
Type of decision rule. Values from Codes where code_tp_cd = 'WOPSRULETP'
ATTRIBUTE_TYPE_CD
VARCHAR2(10)
N
Type of value returned by the rule or entered by the user at the time of validation. Values from Codes where code_tp_cd = 'WOPSRLVLTP'
VALIDATION_REGEX
VARCHAR2(100)
Y
An optional regular expression used to validate the value entered by the user, or returned by the rule.
VALIDATION_REGEX_DES
VARCHAR2(200)
Y
A description of the validation_regex, to facilitate understanding of what the regex is attempting to achieve.
VALIDATION_ERROR_RESOURCE_ID
VARCHAR2(100)
Y

ATTRIBUTE_LABEL
VARCHAR2(100)
Y
A description of the attribute which is displayed on the screen as a label when the user is prompted to enter/select a value. Applies only when RULE_TYPE_CD = 'ENTRYFIELD'
ATTRIBUTE_CODE_TP_CD
VARCHAR2(10)
Y
Used when the user has to select a value from a drop-down: it specifies the code_tp_cd in table Codes that groups the values to be displayed. Applies only when RULE_TYPE_CD = 'ENTRYFIELD' and ATTRIBUTE_TYPE_CD = 'STRING'.
RULE_OPERATION_MML_CD
CHAR(5)
Y
Holds a code which indicates a call to be made to an external system or the Cerillion Network Inventory via the provisioning interface, to retrieve the value associated to this rule; possible options in Codes with Code Type = 'EXCH_ACTON'. Applies only when RULE_TYPE_CD = 'APICALL'
RULE_ATTRIBUTE_MML_COLUMN
VARCHAR2(40)
Y
The name of the mml_decode column containing the output value of the rule.  Applies only when RULE_TYPE_CD = 'APICALL'
RULE_SQL
NCLOB
Y
SQL to be run to retrieve the value associated to this rule.  Applies only when RULE_TYPE_CD = 'DBLOOKUP' .  The SQL must be a SELECT statement returning just one value and and must have the format "SELECT <value/column to be returned> FROM <tables + WHERE condition>". The WHERE condition only recognises the following parameters: :woNo (work order number) and :accountNo (account number).
ACTIVATION_DATE_RULE_YN

RULE_VALIDATION_UID
NUMBER(11, 0)
Y
When the same rule and condition is used on multiple steps, it is only evaluated once on the first step in the group, and the decision is replicated across the steps. If the rule is not satisfied all the steps in the group are immediately marked as skipped; but when the rule is satisfied, only the first step - and any parallel steps - in the group is activated straight-away. The other steps are activated later on without having to run the rule again: this field identifies the outcome of the rule on the first step and it is used for that purpose.   Once the step is activated, this field is blanked. Foreign key to WORK_ORDER_STEP_DECISION.WOSD_UID.
DECISION_RULE_UID
NUMBER(11, 0)
Y
Optional decision rule to be run before activating the step. Foreign key to WORK_ORDER_PROFILE_STEP_RULE.RULE_UID.
DECISION_RULE_EXPECTED_VALUE
CLOB
Y
A condition - written using the syntax of an SQL where clause - which is evaluated when the decision rule is run to determined whether the step can be activated. The value returned by the decision rule should be expressed in the condition as :value e.g. ":value IN ('FA', 'CU')". When the rule's value type is boolean, it should be compared against 'true' or 'false'
ACTIVATE_DATE_RULE_UID
NUMBER(11, 0)
Y
Optional activation date rule to be run before activating the step. Foreign key to WORK_ORDER_PROFILE_STEP_RULE.RULE_UID. It returns a date which is then used with the activate_date_period to calculate the step's activation date.
ACTIVATE_DATE_PERIOD_TP_CD
VARCHAR2(10)
Y
Unit of time in which the activate_date_period is expressed. Values from Codes where code_tp_cd = ACDTPERIOD'
ACTIVATE_DATE_PERIOD
NUMBER(11, 0)
Y
Value added to date returned by the activate date rule to calculate the activation date for the step. Integer greater, equal or lower than 0.

ADDRESSES_LOCAL_TEXT
DDL Code 
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW ADDRESSES_LOCAL_TEXT (PRIME_UID, DISP_ADDRESS_LINE1, DISP_STREET_NO, DISP_STREET_NAME, DISP_PLACE_NAME, DISP_AREA_NAME, DISP_POST_CODE, DISP_FLAT_NO) AS SELECT A.PRIME_UID,          A.DISP_ADDRESS_LINE1,          A.DISP_STREET_NO,          NVL (L.STREET_NAME_LOCAL_TEXT, DISP_STREET_NAME) DISP_STREET_NAME,          NVL (L.LOCALITY_NAME_LOCAL_TEXT, DISP_PLACE_NAME) DISP_PLACE_NAME,          NVL (L.TOWNSHIP_NAME_LOCAL_TEXT, DISP_AREA_NAME) DISP_AREA_NAME,          A.DISP_POST_CODE,          A.DISP_FLAT_NO     FROM LOCALISED_STREET L, ADDRESSES A, ADDRESS_PROFILES AP    WHERE (UPPER (TRIM (A.COUNTRY_NAME)) = 'MALTA' OR A.COUNTRY_NAME IS NULL)      AND A.ADDRESS_PROFILE_UID = AP.ADDRESS_PROFILE_UID AND AP.NAME != 'GO Master' AND AP.NAME != 'GO Other'      AND TRIM (A.STREET_NAME) = TRIM (L.STREET_NAME(+))      AND TRIM (A.AREA_NAME) = TRIM (L.TOWNSHIP_NAME(+))      AND TRIM (NVL (TRIM (A.PLACE_NAME), 'BLANK')) = TRIM (NVL (L.LOCALITY_NAME(+), 'BLANK'))UNION   SELECT A.PRIME_UID,          A.DISP_ADDRESS_LINE1,          A.DISP_STREET_NO,          NVL (MA.STREET_NAME_LOCAL_TEXT, DISP_STREET_NAME) DISP_STREET_NAME,          NVL (MA.PLACE_NAME_LOCAL_TEXT, DISP_PLACE_NAME) DISP_PLACE_NAME,          NVL (MA.AREA_NAME_LOCAL_TEXT, DISP_AREA_NAME) DISP_AREA_NAME,          A.DISP_POST_CODE,          A.DISP_FLAT_NO     FROM ADDRESSES A, ADDRESS_PROFILES AP, MASTER_ADDRESSES MA    WHERE (UPPER (TRIM (A.COUNTRY_NAME)) = 'MALTA' OR A.COUNTRY_NAME IS NULL)      AND A.ADDRESS_PROFILE_UID = AP.ADDRESS_PROFILE_UID      AND AP.ADDRESS_PROFILE_UID IN       (SELECT REGEXP_SUBSTR((SELECT SYSTEM_PARAMETERS.PARAM_VALUE_CHARACTER FROM SYSTEM_PARAMETERS WHERE SYSTEM_PARAMETERS.PARAM_CODE = 'LNKMD'),'[^,]+', 1, LEVEL) FROM DUALCONNECT BY REGEXP_SUBSTR((SELECT SYSTEM_PARAMETERS.PARAM_VALUE_CHARACTER FROM SYSTEM_PARAMETERS WHERE SYSTEM_PARAMETERS.PARAM_CODE = 'LNKMD'), '[^,]+', 1, LEVEL) IS NOT NULL)      AND A.EXTERNAL_UID = MA.EXTERNAL_UIDUNIONSELECT PRIME_UID,       DISP_ADDRESS_LINE1,       DISP_STREET_NO,       DISP_STREET_NAME,       DISP_PLACE_NAME,       DISP_AREA_NAME,       DISP_POST_CODE,       DISP_FLAT_NO FROM (   SELECT   A.PRIME_UID AS PRIME_UID,            A.DISP_ADDRESS_LINE1 AS DISP_ADDRESS_LINE1,            A.DISP_STREET_NO AS DISP_STREET_NO,            NVL (MA.STREET_NAME_LOCAL_TEXT, DISP_STREET_NAME)               DISP_STREET_NAME,            NVL (MA.PLACE_NAME_LOCAL_TEXT, DISP_PLACE_NAME) DISP_PLACE_NAME,            NVL (MA.AREA_NAME_LOCAL_TEXT, DISP_AREA_NAME) DISP_AREA_NAME,            A.DISP_POST_CODE AS DISP_POST_CODE,            A.DISP_FLAT_NO AS DISP_FLAT_NO,            ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY A.PRIME_UID ORDER BY PRIME_UID) AS ROWNUMBER     FROM   ADDRESSES A, ADDRESS_PROFILES AP, MASTER_ADDRESSES MA    WHERE   (UPPER (TRIM (A.COUNTRY_NAME)) = 'MALTA'             OR A.COUNTRY_NAME IS NULL)            AND A.ADDRESS_PROFILE_UID = AP.ADDRESS_PROFILE_UID            AND NVL(A.AREA_NAME, 'EMPTY_AREA') = NVL(MA.AREA_NAME, 'EMPTY_AREA')            AND NVL(A.PLACE_NAME, 'EMPTY_PLACE') = NVL(MA.PLACE_NAME, 'EMPTY_PLACE')            AND NVL(A.STREET_NAME, 'EMPTY_STREET') = NVL(MA.STREET_NAME, 'EMPTY_STREET')            AND NVL(A.POST_CODE, 'EMPTY_POSTCODE') = NVL(MA.POST_CODE, 'EMPTY_POSTCODE')            AND AP.ADDRESS_PROFILE_UID IN       (SELECT REGEXP_SUBSTR((SELECT SYSTEM_PARAMETERS.PARAM_VALUE_CHARACTER FROM SYSTEM_PARAMETERS WHERE SYSTEM_PARAMETERS.PARAM_CODE = 'MAMAE'),'[^,]+', 1, LEVEL) FROM DUALCONNECT BY REGEXP_SUBSTR((SELECT SYSTEM_PARAMETERS.PARAM_VALUE_CHARACTER FROM SYSTEM_PARAMETERS WHERE SYSTEM_PARAMETERS.PARAM_CODE = 'MAMAE'), '[^,]+', 1, LEVEL) IS NOT NULL)) WHERE ROWNUMBER = 1UNION   SELECT A.PRIME_UID,          A.DISP_ADDRESS_LINE1,          A.DISP_STREET_NO,          A.DISP_STREET_NAME,          A.DISP_PLACE_NAME,          A.DISP_AREA_NAME,          A.DISP_POST_CODE, MV_BAL_TARIFF_CATEGORY
DDL Code 
CREATE OR REPLACE FORCE VIEW MV_BAL_TARIFF_CATEGORY(   TARIFF_CODE_UID,   TARIFF_TP_CD,   TRANS_CODE,   CATEGORY_NAME)AS   SELECT   ut.TARIFF_CODE_UID,            ut.tariff_tp_cd,            ut.TRANS_CODE,            BAND_DES AS CATEGORY_NAME     FROM   usage_tariffs ut, gsm_distance_bands gdb    WHERE   ut.BAND_NO = gdb.BAND_NO AND ut.tariff_tp_cd = 'GC'   UNION   SELECT   ut.TARIFF_CODE_UID,            ut.tariff_tp_cd,            ut.TRANS_CODE,            c_et.EVENT_TYPE_DESC || ' - ' || c_ea.EVENT_ACTION_DESC               AS CATEGORY_NAME            --|| ' (' || tariff_code_uid || ')'     FROM   event_types c_et, event_actions c_ea, usage_tariffs ut    WHERE       c_et.EVENT_TYPE_ID = ut.EVENT_TYPE_ID            AND c_ea.EVENT_ACTION_ID = ut.EVENT_ACTION_ID            AND ut.tariff_tp_cd = 'GE'   UNION   SELECT   ut.TARIFF_CODE_UID,            ut.tariff_tp_cd,            ut.TRANS_CODE,            'Roam (' || gc.OPERATOR_NAME || ')' AS CATEGORY_NAME     FROM   usage_tariffs ut, gsm_correspondents gc    WHERE       ut.tariff_tp_cd = 'GT'            AND gc.IMSI_COUNTRY_CODE = ut.IMSI_COUNTRY_CODE            AND gc.IMSI_NETWORK_CODE = ut.IMSI_NETWORK_CODE   UNION   SELECT   ut.TARIFF_CODE_UID,            ut.tariff_tp_cd,            ut.TRANS_CODE,            'Other (' || tariff_code_uid || ')' AS CATEGORY_NAME     FROM   usage_tariffs ut    WHERE   ut.tariff_tp_cd NOT IN ('GE', 'GC', 'GT');

USER_ACCESS
DDL Code 
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW USER_ACCESS("INGRES_USERNAME", "FUNCTION_CODE", "QUERY_YN", "CREATE_YN", "UPDATE_YN", "DELETE_YN") ASSELECT UAA.INGRES_USERNAME, UAA.FUNCTION_CODE, CASE   WHEN (FUNFRROLE.QUERY_YN = 'N' AND UAA.QUERY_YN = 'N') THEN 'N'  WHEN (FUNFRROLE.QUERY_YN = 'Y' AND UAA.QUERY_YN = 'N') THEN 'Y'  ELSE UAA.QUERY_YN END AS QUERY_YN, CASE   WHEN (FUNFRROLE.CREATE_YN = 'N' AND UAA.CREATE_YN = 'N') THEN 'N'  WHEN (FUNFRROLE.CREATE_YN = 'Y' AND UAA.CREATE_YN = 'N') THEN 'Y'  ELSE UAA.CREATE_YN END AS CREATE_YN, CASE   WHEN (FUNFRROLE.UPDATE_YN = 'N' AND UAA.UPDATE_YN = 'N') THEN 'N'  WHEN (FUNFRROLE.UPDATE_YN = 'Y' AND UAA.UPDATE_YN = 'N') THEN 'Y'  ELSE UAA.UPDATE_YN END AS UPDATE_YN, CASE   WHEN (FUNFRROLE.DELETE_YN = 'N' AND UAA.DELETE_YN = 'N') THEN 'N'  WHEN (FUNFRROLE.DELETE_YN = 'Y' AND UAA.DELETE_YN = 'N') THEN 'Y'  ELSE UAA.DELETE_YN END AS DELETE_YNFROM USER_EXTENDED_ACCESS UAA LEFT OUTER JOIN  USER_ROLE USERROLE ON USERROLE.INGRES_USERNAME = UAA.INGRES_USERNAME LEFT OUTER JOIN FUNCTION_FOR_ROLE FUNFRROLE  ON FUNFRROLE.ROLE_UID = USERROLE.ROLE_UID AND FUNFRROLE.FUNCTION_CODE = UAA.FUNCTION_CODEUNIONSELECT USERROLE.INGRES_USERNAME, FUNFRROLE.FUNCTION_CODE, CASE   WHEN (FUNFRROLE.QUERY_YN = 'N' AND UAA.QUERY_YN = 'N') THEN 'N'  WHEN (FUNFRROLE.QUERY_YN = 'N' AND UAA.QUERY_YN = 'Y') THEN 'Y'  ELSE FUNFRROLE.QUERY_YN END AS QUERY_YN, CASE   WHEN (FUNFRROLE.CREATE_YN = 'N' AND UAA.CREATE_YN = 'N') THEN 'N'  WHEN (FUNFRROLE.CREATE_YN = 'N' AND UAA.CREATE_YN = 'Y') THEN 'Y'  ELSE FUNFRROLE.CREATE_YN END AS CREATE_YN, CASE   WHEN (FUNFRROLE.UPDATE_YN = 'N' AND UAA.UPDATE_YN = 'N') THEN 'N'  WHEN (FUNFRROLE.UPDATE_YN = 'N' AND UAA.UPDATE_YN = 'Y') THEN 'Y'  ELSE FUNFRROLE.UPDATE_YN END AS UPDATE_YN, CASE   WHEN (FUNFRROLE.DELETE_YN = 'N' AND UAA.DELETE_YN = 'N') THEN 'N'  WHEN (FUNFRROLE.DELETE_YN = 'N' AND UAA.DELETE_YN = 'Y') THEN 'Y'  ELSE FUNFRROLE.DELETE_YN END AS DELETE_YN FROM USER_ROLE USERROLEINNER JOIN FUNCTION_FOR_ROLE FUNFRROLE  ON FUNFRROLE.ROLE_UID = USERROLE.ROLE_UIDLEFT OUTER JOIN USER_EXTENDED_ACCESS UAA ON USERROLE.INGRES_USERNAME = UAA.INGRES_USERNAME  AND FUNFRROLE.FUNCTION_CODE = UAA.FUNCTION_CODE
USER_DEFINED_COLUMN_JSON_VIEW
DDL Code 
CREATE OR REPLACE FORCE EDITIONABLE VIEW SUPER.USER_DEFINED_COLUMN_JSON_VIEW (TABLE_NAME,PARTICIPANT_UID,UDFS) AS SELECT table_name, participant_uid,JSON_ARRAYAGG( JSON_OBJECT('col' VALUE column_name,            'vstr' VALUE CONVERT(column_value_string, 'utf8'), 'vdob' VALUE column_value_double,'vint' VALUE column_value_int,'vdate' VALUE column_value_date             ABSENT ON NULL)) AS UDFS FROM  user_defined_column GROUP BY table_name,participant_uid/
